CHINA PRESS

Another Denial
Mr. L. Riggio, leader of the Italian Fascisti in
Shanghai, denies that the local followers of Il Duce
have devised ways and means of "liquidating" the
writer.
It will be recalled that I remarked in a recent
broadcast that I had received a number of threaten-
ing letters, purporting to come from Shanghai Fas-
cists.
One of these letters stated that the local Fascist
Party had decided, at a recent meeting, to remove
me from the local scene. The exact method had
not been worked out but when this detail had been
taken care of, swift action was promised.
I have received other letters of a similar nature,
also signed by persons claiming to be Fascists. And
on several occasions my movements at night have
been followed by persons riding in motorcars, the
ownership of which has been traced to local Fascists.
Naturally, Riggio couldn't do anything else but
issue a denial. But the fact remains that it took
him about ten days after I had reported the incidents
to get his denial written and in printed form. It
appeared in the April 2 issue of the Italian Daily
News, a four-page bulletin devoted to the publishing
of official Italian news agency dispatches.
However, Riggio lets it be known that he doesn't
approve of me, says I abuse and slander the totalitar-
ians, which is something, he points out, that the
totalitarians never do.
Oh Yeah!

《字林西报》（China Press）

再次否认
L. 里焦（L. Riggio，音译）先生，上海意大利法西斯分子的头目，否认当地“领袖”（Il Duce）的追随者已想出“清除”这位作家的方法和手段。
读者或许还记得，我在最近的一次广播中提到，我收到了一些恐吓信，声称来自上海法西斯分子。
其中一封信称，当地法西斯党在最近的一次会议上决定将我从本地舞台上移除。具体方法尚未制定，但一旦细节敲定，承诺将采取迅速行动。
我还收到了其他类似性质的信件，同样由自称是法西斯分子的人签署。此外，有几次我在夜间的行踪被乘坐汽车的人跟踪，这些车辆的所有权经查证属于当地法西斯分子。
自然，里焦除了发表否认声明外别无他法。但事实是，在我报告这些事件后，他花了大约十天时间才写好并刊印了他的否认声明。该声明刊登在4月2日的《意大利每日新闻》（Italian Daily News）上，这是一份四页的公告，专门发布意大利官方通讯社的电讯。
然而，里焦让人知道他不赞成我，说我辱骂和诽谤极权主义者，他指出，极权主义者从不这样做。
哦，是吗！

No. S. B. D. 681/40
Date December 23, 1940

Subject Interference with Radio Station XMHA, 445 Racecourse Road (American).

Made by D. S. I. MacAdie Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

At 4 p.m. on 16.12.40, it came to the notice
of the management of Radio Station, XMHA (American),
445 Racecourse Road, that some unknown person was
jamming the station's broadcast by broadcasting a
harsh buzzing noise on the same wavelength, i.e.
K.C. 600. The management of the station immediately
countered this interference by broadcasting from
another transmitter on wavelength K.C. 640. The
latter wavelength was also interfered with, whereupon
X.M.H.A. put a "harmonic" on K.C. 650 on one of its
transmitters so that the broadcast from the Station
was going out on three wavelengths. The Station
also broadcasts on the 25 metre band (short wave)
but a few days later jamming commenced on this
wavelength. The interference has been
continued regularly since 16.12.40 and according
to the management of XMHA, is directed to compelling
the station to reduce its power output from 350
watts to 200 watts. This, the station management
refuse to do, as it would reduce the advertising
value of the broadcasts. It appears that in May,
1940, XMHA was in receipt of a letter from Major
Asano of the Radio Control Office (Japanese)
requesting a reduction of the power output but
his request was refused. Other local stations
were similarly requested and the majority of them

1940年12月16日下午4时，跑马厅路445号 XMHA 广播电台（美资）的管理层注意到，有不明身份者在同一波长（即千周 600）上广播刺耳的嗡嗡声，干扰该台的广播。电台管理层立即通过另一台发射机在千周 640 波长上进行广播，以 counter 这种干扰。后者波长也受到了干扰，随后 XMHA 在其中一台发射机上于千周 650 加载了“谐波”，使得该台的广播同时在三个波长上播出。该台还在25米波段（短波）进行广播，但几天后，该波长也开始受到干扰。自1940年12月16日以来，干扰一直定期进行，据 XMHA 管理层称，其目的是迫使该台将输出功率从350瓦降低到200瓦。电台管理层拒绝这样做，因为这会降低广播的广告价值。据悉，1940年5月，XMHA 曾收到日本无线电管制办公室浅野少校（Major Asano）的一封信，要求降低输出功率，但该请求被拒绝。其他本地电台也收到了类似要求，其中大多数

DEC 2, 1940
Radio Shoho Lo

Radio Jamming
Continues Here

U.S. Waits Japanese
Reply To Protest
On Interference

Interference with station
XMHA's broadcasts continued un-
abated today with Japanese offi-
cials still delaying an answer to
the American Consulate's protest
against the jamming of news re-
ports by the American station.
A spokesman for the Japanese
Consulate said he expected an
answer would be given sometime
this week and that the matter
would be amicably settled. He
said, however, that settlement of
XMHA's complaint would not
necessarily mean a settlement of
basic "differences of views."
An official of the station, com-
menting on recurrent rumors that
XMHA intends to retaliate by in-
terfering with Japanese broad-
casts, said today, "We haven't re-
taliated at all." He said that the
station's broadcasts were inter-
fered with all day yesterday and
this morning although the inter-
ference was "not awfully effective"
on the short wave lengths.

无线电干扰
在此持续

美国等待日本
对干扰抗议的
回复

对 XMHA 电台广播的干扰今天仍在继续，未有减弱，日本官员仍拖延回复美国领事馆关于美方电台新闻报道受到干扰的抗议。
日本领事馆发言人表示，预计本周内会给出答复，此事将得到友好解决。但他表示，解决 XMHA 的投诉并不一定意味着基本“观点分歧”的解决。
电台一位官员就有关 XMHA 打算通过干扰日本广播进行报复的反复谣言评论道：“我们根本没有进行报复。”他说，昨天全天和今天上午，该台的广播都受到了干扰，尽管在短波波长上的干扰“效果并不是非常显著”。

11884

Radio Jamming:
How to Circumvent

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—It is assumed that the opera-
tion of the various Broadcasting
Stations here in Shanghai is perfectly
legal and in accordance with the
franchise issued them by the
authorities. If they infringe any re-
gulation it is natural to suppose that
their licence would either be sus-
pended or a fine imposed.

To resort to "jamming" leaves me
with the opinion that the "jammer"
is either some person, persons, or
organization having a grudge against
a particular station and appears to
be well-protected in that the "jam-
ming" would continue until such
time as it is stopped.

If my memory serves me rightly
three local stations have had, and
XMHA is now having, this taste of
distorted harmony. Why not organize?
It is a very simple matter to defeat
the "jammers" at their own game.
Needless to add, other stations may
yet be favoured after XMHA has
had its ether purified. Why not then
come to an understanding that in
the event of one or more stations
being jammed, the others rebroadcast
the particular part of that programme
to which exception has been taken.
In the case of XMHA I presume it
is our good friend Carroll Alcott,
well then, at 8 a.m., 1 p.m. 8 p.m.
and 10 p.m. when Mr. Alcott is on
the air, one of the stations has a
direct line to him and the others
rebroadcast it by picking up that
station with their receivers. This
eliminates the necessity of several
lines, which I understand is quite
an expensive item. By this method
the station that is being jammed is
more or less heard all over the dial.
Financial arrangements and details
governing such rebroadcast is certain-
ly not an insurmountable obstacle.

Regarding the jamming on short-
waves or medium waves for distant
points of reception, I doubt very
much if the present method is
effective, such jamming generally is
done at the point of reception rather
than that of transmission.

C. MASC.
Shanghai, Dec. 20.

A Fund Suggested
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—May another Briton add his
endorsement of the excellent letter
appearing in your to-day's issue on
"Jamming by Japanese."

For me, and many other minor
Shanghai citizens, albeit probably
none the less intellectual, Carroll
Alcott, with all respect to our own
officialdom, is our daily Ministry of
Information.

Many have come to regard Mr.
Alcott as the most popular exponent
of Democracy in Shanghai, and,
therefore, worthy of all possible
support to combat the Axis pro-
paganda and falsehoods belched forth
from some local stations. To my
knowledge his voice is eagerly looked
forward to all over China and else-
where in the Far East.

I would be only too glad to con-
tribute to any fund either towards
minimizing the station's losses or for
the purpose of a counter-attack.

D'ARNUM
Shanghai, Dec. 21.

Alleged Statement Denied
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—There appears in today's issue
of the "North China Daily News," a
news article headed "Protest Lodged
in XMHA Jamming." In the second
paragraph of this article appears a
statement reported to have been
made by me.

At this time I wish to deny having
made any such statement and to
assure you that when I am ready to
make a statement as Managing
Director of Radio Station XMHA, I
will forward such statement to you
over my signature.

E. H. HEALEY,
Managing Director.
Shanghai, Dec. 21.

无线电干扰：
如何规避

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——假定上海这里各家广播电台的运营是完全合法的，并符合当局颁发的特许状规定。如果它们违反任何规章，自然可以认为它们的执照将被暂停或处以罚款。

诉诸“干扰”让我觉得，“干扰者”要么是对特定电台怀恨在心的某个人、某些人或组织，而且似乎受到很好的保护，因为“干扰”会一直持续，直到被制止为止。

如果我的记忆没错，本地有三家电台曾经尝过这种失真和谐的滋味，而 XMHA 现在正经历着。为什么不联合起来呢？要以其人之道还治其人之身，击败“干扰者”是非常简单的事情。毋庸赘言，在 XMHA 的电波被净化后，其他电台可能还会受到青睐。那么，何不达成谅解，一旦一家或多家电台受到干扰，其他电台就重播那些引起异议的节目部分。以 XMHA 为例，我想是我们的好朋友卡罗尔·奥尔科特（Carroll Alcott），那么，在奥尔科特先生播出的上午8时、下午1时、晚上8时和晚上10时，其中一家电台与他直通连线，其他电台则通过接收该机信号进行重播。这就消除了对多条线路的需求，据我所知，这是一笔相当昂贵的开支。通过这种方法，受到干扰的电台或多或少能在整个波段被听到。 governing such rebroadcast（管理此类重播的）财务安排和细节肯定不是不可克服的障碍。

关于针对远距离接收点的短波或中波干扰，我非常怀疑目前的方法是否有效，此类干扰通常是在接收点而非发射点进行的。

C. MASC.
上海，12月20日。

建议设立基金
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——另一位英国人可否在此附议贵报今日刊登的关于“日本人的干扰”的优秀来信。

对我以及许多其他上海小市民来说，尽管智力上可能毫不逊色，但卡罗尔·奥尔科特，尽管我们要尊重我们自己的官方机构，他是我们的日常新闻部长。

许多人开始视奥尔科特先生为上海最受欢迎的民主倡导者，因此，值得给予一切可能的支持，以对抗轴心国宣传和一些本地电台喷吐出的谎言。据我所知，全中国乃至远东其他地区的人都急切地期待听到他的声音。

我非常乐意为任何旨在尽量减少电台损失或用于反击的基金捐款。

D'ARNUM
上海，12月21日。

否认所谓声明
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——今日《字林西报》刊登了一篇题为“就 XMHA 受干扰提出抗议”的新闻文章。在该文章的第二段中，出现了一则据称是我发表的声明。

在此，我要否认曾发表过任何此类声明，并向您保证，当我作为 XMHA 广播电台总经理准备发表声明时，我将签署后发送给您。

E. H. 希利（E. H. HEALEY），
总经理。
上海，12月21日。

12860

DEC 21 1940

Radio Jamming
Under Scrutiny
By Japanese

"Representations have been received from the United States Consulate-General" regarding the differences in views existing between Station XMHA and the Japanese Radio Control Board, a Japanese Embassy spokesman confirmed yesterday afternoon at a regular press conference.

The spokesman added that the Japanese authorities are "studying" the representations.

There has been a "disagreement in views" between Station XMHA and the Japanese Radio Control Board and conversations are in progress to seek an amicable solution, the spokesman declared.

Healey's Blast Referred To

He then referred to an item carried by a local English-language paper quoting Mr. F. L. Healey, managing director of the station, as saying, "the United States has the most powerful equipment in the world. We could blow them (the Japanese) off the map."

Such remarks, the spokesman emphasized, certainly will not contribute to an amicable settlement of the question. The spokesman added, however, he believed that the alleged remarks credited by the paper to Mr. Healey were a "misquotation."

The spokesman declared further that though he did not know whether or not freedom of speech was peace, he did know that to refrain from abuse of the use of freedom of speech was a basis for peace.

Freedom Of Speech Abused

There must be limits to everything including freedom of speech, the spokesman declared. He referred to an editorial carried by one of Shanghai papers not long ago, alleging Shanghai was moving towards "anarchy" under a "Nippon-sponsored new order," and declared that such remarks were beyond the limits of freedom of speech. On the question regarding the details of the problem, the spokesman declined to comment.

"Representations have been received from the United States Consulate-General" regarding the differences in views existing between Station XMHA and the Japanese Radio Control Board, a Japanese Embassy spokesman confirmed yesterday afternoon at a regular press conference.

The spokesman added that the Japanese authorities were "studying" the representations.

There has been a "disagreement in views" between Station XMHA and the Japanese Radio Control Board and conversations are in progress to seek an amicable solution, the spokesman declared.

Such remarks, the spokesman emphasized, certainly will not contribute to an amicable settlement of the question. The spokesman added, however, he believed that the alleged remarks credited by the paper to Mr. Healey were a "misquotation."

The spokesman declared further that though he did not know whether or not freedom of speech was peace, he did know that to refrain from abuse of the freedom of speech was a basis for peace.

There must be a limit to everything, including freedom of speech, the spokesman declared. He referred to an editorial carried by one of Shanghai papers not long ago, alleging Shanghai was moving towards "anarchy" under a "Nippon-sponsored new order," and declared that such remarks were beyond the limits of freedom of speech. On the question regarding the details of the problem the spokesman declined to comment.

Asked by an American correspondent, "Do I gather that the Japanese admit that they are jamming the station?" the spokesman declared, "I only meant what I said. I have not been informed of the source of the jamming."

CHINA
DEC 1

Alcott Booms On
XMHA Lodges
Protest On
Radio Jamming

Barely audible above the vibrant whirr of a high frequency oscillator, the voice of Newscaster Carrol D. Alcott continued to boom from Radio Station XMHA yesterday, while the U.S. Consulate-General continued to consider a written protest lodged by the owners of the radio station.

Despite the persistent jamming, which started two days ago, no abatement was noticed in the tone of Mr. Alcott's pro-democratic tirades. Speaking through a storm of interference yesterday afternoon and evening, he continued to lay the blame for the jamming at the door of the "Japanese Radio Control Board."

Protesting on what he termed an "attempted Japanese effort to limit the power output of most broadcasting stations in Shanghai to 200 watts," Mr. E. L. Healey, American owner of XMHA, lodged a written protest with the U.S. Consulate-General here yesterday morning. The protest was being considered late yesterday afternoon.

The radio interference is believed to be aimed at local anti-Axis broadcasts in general and Carrol Alcott's pungent news commentaries in particular. Also jammed by the alleged Japanese radio beam yesterday were the news and music broadcasts in the German language over the same station. These broadcasts are reportedly directed at the local Jewish refugee population.

The Japanese Radio Control Board, according to some reports, has attempted during the past few months to limit the power output of radio stations in Shanghai to 200 watts. Stations which refused to comply with the "requests" were jammed over the air, these reports state.

“干扰”持续

称日本方面负责。

强制性的“要求”

然而，该法国电台继续保持其正常输出功率，且在過去几天内，对该电台广播的干扰已减弱。

Interference Jams
Alcott Broadcast

Block On American Radio Station XMHA
Said Traced To Japanese Warship
In Whangpoo; Consul Informed

The radio jam which has been intermittently blasting out station XMHA's broadcasts on 600 kilocycles since 4 p.m. yesterday has been traced to a Japanese warship in the Whangpoo, Mr. E. L. Healey, manager of the station, told the Shanghai Evening Post today.

Mr. Healey has notified the American Consulate-General here of the latest interference with the American station's broadcasting program.

Aimed at Mr. Carroll D. Alcott, outspoken radio news commentator who broadcasts three times daily over XMHA, this is the

Jam Still On

At 1 p.m. today the jam on the Radio Station X.M.H.A., 600 kilocycles, which started yesterday at 4 p.m. was still on and listeners to the Carroll Alcott news broadcast had to turn their dials to 640 kilocycles in order to hear his voice.

second time that the station has been interfered with. It will be recalled that the station suffered a similar occurrence last Spring.

Japanese Demands

It is believed that the radio blockade was imposed on the station because the American management refused to comply with demands of the Japanese Radio Control Board to cut the power output to 200 watts and submit news for censorship.

Mr. Healey said that he had received a letter from the superintendent of the board, Major Asano, in which these demands were put forth. The letter emanated from the Nanking Road office of the board in the Settlement.

In a broadcast three weeks ago Mr. Alcott intimated that a jam of the station's frequency was forthcoming. During the past three weeks, however, the block was directed against the French

radio station FFZ, from which station it was yesterday transferred to XMHA.

Lifted Few Minutes

The interference was lifted for a few minutes last night when Mr. Alcott started his 10.15 broadcast. For three or four minutes reception was clear, during which time Mr. Alcott told his listeners of the reason for the jam and who was responsible for it.

Shortly after Mr. Alcott had advised listeners that they could hear him on 630 or 640 kilocycles the jam was again enforced, drowning out the station entirely. Reception on 640 kilocycles, however, was clear.

No interference was evident as Alcott gave his 8 o'clock broadcast this morning, but Mr. Healey said that he expected the jam to be resumed later in the day.

Station Prepared

The station, Mr. Healey declared was prepared to meet the emergency, however, and would broadcast simultaneously on 600 and 640 kilocycles and 25 meters.

Mr. Frank P. Lockhart, American Consul-General in Shanghai told the Shanghai Evening Post this morning that he had been informed of the interference yesterday and that he was awaiting an official protest on the matter before taking action.

Mr. Healey declared today that he would continue to fight the Control Board, and jam or no jam, would not give in to their demands.

（批：2）

该电台经理E. L. Healey先生今日告诉《上海晚邮报》，自昨日下午4时起间歇性阻断XMHA电台600千周广播的无线电干扰，已被追踪到位于黄浦江上的一艘日本军舰。

此次干扰针对的是Carroll D. Alcott先生，他是一位直言不讳的无线电新闻评论员，每日通过XMHA广播三次，这是

干扰仍在继续

今日下午1时，始于昨日下午4时的对X.M.H.A.电台600千周的干扰仍在持续，收听Carroll Alcott新闻广播的听众不得不将旋钮调至640千周才能听到他的声音。

该电台第二次受到干扰。人们还记得，去年春天该电台曾发生过类似事件。

日本方面的要求

据信，对该电台实施无线电封锁是因为美方管理层拒绝服从日本无线电管理委员会的要求，即把输出功率降至200瓦并提交新闻接受审查。

Healey先生说，他收到了该委员会主管浅野少校（Major Asano，音译）的一封信，信中提出了这些要求。该信发自公共租界南京路的委员会办公室。

在三周前的一次广播中，Alcott先生暗示该电台频率即将受到干扰。然而，在过去三周里，封锁是针对法国

广播电台FFZ进行的，昨天才从该台转移到了XMHA。

短暂解除

昨晚当Alcott先生开始其10点15分的广播时，干扰解除了几分钟。有三四分钟的时间接收清晰，在此期间，Alcott先生向听众说明了干扰的原因及责任方。

在Alcott先生建议听众可以在630或640千周收听他之后不久，干扰再次实施，完全淹没了该电台的信号。然而，640千周的接收是清晰的。

今早Alcott进行8点钟广播时，没有明显的干扰，但Healey先生说，他预计当天晚些时候干扰会恢复。

电台已做好准备

Healey先生宣称，电台已准备好应对紧急情况，将在600和640千周以及25米波段同时广播。

美国驻上海总领事Frank P. Lockhart先生今早告诉《上海晚邮报》，他已于昨日获悉干扰情况，在就此事项采取正式抗议行动之前，他正在等待官方抗议书。

Healey先生今日宣称，他将继续与管委会斗争，无论是否有干扰，都不会屈服于他们的要求。

page_data.en:
More Jam
After eight months of comparative freedom from interference, the jam is again being spread on the broadcast wave length of Station XMHA. The French station in Shanghai, FFZ, also is receiving considerable interference from outside quarters
The usual theories have been advanced by listeners concerning the reasons back of the jamming. Many have argued that the Axis is back of the interference. This is definitely not the case.
The local Japanese Radio Control Board has made no effort to hide its responsibility for the jamming. During the past eight or nine months, the majority of radio stations in Shanghai have been notified by the board that it would appreciate submission to its control. The stations have been requested to reduce their power output to 200 watts.
At first, most of the stations refused. They soon found their wave lengths being interfered with. Music broadcasts were drowned out by a harsh buzzing noise. Speech could be heard but the background buzzing made it unpleasant to listen to. Eventually, the stations started succumbing to the desires of the control board. They reduced their power outputs.
Two stations which have not yet submitted to this control are XMHA and FFZ. At least, these are the only two stations being jammed at the present time.
The "jam" was placed on the French station about one month ago after it had been lifted on Station XMHD, of the Shanghai Christian Broadcasting Association. It has been on FFZ ever since.
The "jam" went back on XMHA two days ago and just how long it will continue is a matter of speculation. Officials of the station tell me they plan a protest which should be forthcoming in a day or
two. They also state that they have no intention of submitting to a control that will not permit their broadcasts to be heard very far beyond Shanghai.

Celebration
Reports from the western district of the International Settlement indicate that the China Club, big-time gambling casino, gave the customers quite a blow-out when it re-opened for business last Saturday night after two weeks of blockade.
More than $8,000 was spent on free food, customers were given $5,000 worth of free cigars and cigarettes. The cost for American oranges alone Saturday evening was $900. Boys had a busy time sweeping up orange peels.

Complaint
A local Italian big-wig complains in a note to myself that his telephone is kept busy by persons inquiring about the route the British will take to invade the industrial areas of Northern Italy. The thing to do in such a case is either to cut the telephone wires or refuse to pay the phone bill and let the telephone company do the disconnecting.
page_data.zh:
更多干扰

在相对自由地免受干扰八个月之后，干扰再次蔓延至XMHA电台的广播波长。上海的法国电台FFZ也受到了来自外部的大量干扰

听众们就干扰背后的原因提出了通常的理论。许多人认为轴心国是干扰的幕后黑手。事实绝非如此。

当地日本无线电管理委员会并未试图掩盖其对干扰的责任。在过去八九个月里，上海的大多数广播电台都收到委员会的通知，表示希望它们服从其管制。各电台被要求将输出功率降低至200瓦。

起初，大多数电台拒绝配合。它们很快发现自己的波长受到干扰。音乐广播被刺耳的嗡嗡声淹没。虽然能听到讲话声，但背景的嗡嗡声使得收听体验令人不快。最终，各电台开始顺从管理委员会的意愿。它们降低了输出功率。

目前尚未屈从于这种管制的两家电台是XMHA和FFZ。至少，这是目前仅有的两家受到干扰的电台。

大约一个月前，在上海基督教广播协会所属的XMHD电台解除干扰后，“干扰”被施加于法国电台。自此一直持续在FFZ电台上。

两天前，“干扰”重新回到XMHA电台，它将持续多久尚属猜测。电台官员告诉我，他们计划提出抗议，预计在一两天内发出。他们还表示，无意屈从于一种不允许其广播传播到上海以外很远地区的管制。

庆祝活动

来自公共租界西区的报告表明，大型赌博赌场中国俱乐部（China Club）在封锁两周后于上周六晚重新营业时，为顾客提供了一场盛大的款待。

免费食物花费超过8,000美元，顾客获得了价值5,000美元的免费雪茄和香烟。仅周六晚上的美国橙子一项就花费了900美元。侍者们忙着清扫橙子皮。

投诉

一位当地意大利大人物在给本人的一张便条中抱怨说，他的电话一直占线，因为有人询问英国军队入侵意大利北部工业区的路线。在这种情况下，要么切断电话线，要么拒绝支付电话费，让电话公司去断线。

D.6812/14/X(1)-
30 12 40

Chinese-American Weekly Review dated December 23 :-

FAILURE OF THE CONTROL OF BROADCASTING
（批：File
min. Xu HA）

As a matter of fact, the world has long ago been well informed of the aggressive acts of Japan in China during the past few years and of her acts in the occupied areas. Despite this, the Japanese are still trying to hoodwink the world by detaining all news disadvantageous to them with improper procedure, so that such news may not spread throughout the world.

In April this year, XHA, a local American broadcasting station, was interfered with and because of the interference, it changed its wave length from 600 to 650, but the disturbing sound could still be heard. Investigations showed that the disturbing sound came from Hongkew for at that time, Mr. Alcott broadcast about the re-election of the members of the S.M.C. and the Japanese, in a desire to make more seats on the Council, resorted to unlawful procedure to interfere with the broadcasts.

In July this year, the Japanese sponsored elements ordered the expulsion of seven well-known foreign newspapermen including Mr. Alcott. In addition, the Japanese rang up the broadcasting station where Mr. Alcott was a broadcaster, warning him to stop broadcasting within three days. However, Mr. Alcott, apart from making a report to the American Consulate-General and the Police, carried on his broadcasting work.

Recently, the Japanese repeated their old trick. XHA was interfered with again on December 16 and the interfering sound came from a Japanese warship berthed in the Whangpoo. It is because the Japanese are thinking to control foreign-owned broadcasting stations in Shanghai, to request these stations to reduce their power to under 200 watts and to apply for registration. As the attempt ended in failure, XHA was the first that was interfered with, FFZ came next and then the American broadcasting station was interfered with again. The owner of the latter named station firmly indicated that he would never surrender.

It is quite clear that the Japanese desire to exercise control of foreign-owned broadcasting stations in Shanghai for these stations are in the habit of broadcasting correct news which are obviously disadvantageous to Japan. The movements of Japan supply news commentators with the best materials. Instead of ceasing their acts of aggression, the Japanese desire to exercise control over broadcasting stations. It will only supply these stations with more materials for news.
page_data.zh:
D.6812/14/X(1)-
30 12 40

12月23日出版的《中美周刊》：-

广播管制的失败
（批：归档
徐HA部长）

事实上，世界早已充分了解日本过去几年在中国的侵略行径及其在占领区的行为。尽管如此，日本人仍试图通过不当手段扣留所有对其不利的新闻，以欺骗世界，使此类新闻无法传遍全球。

今年四月，本地美国广播电台XHA受到干扰，因受干扰，其波长从600改为650，但仍能听到干扰噪音。调查显示，干扰噪音来自虹口，因为当时Alcott先生正在广播关于工部局董事改选的消息，而日本人为了在董事会中获得更多席位，采取了非法手段干扰广播。

今年七月，日本支持的势力下令驱逐包括Alcott先生在内的七名知名外国记者。此外，日本人打电话给Alcott先生担任播音员的广播电台，警告他在三天内停止广播。然而，Alcott先生除了向美国总领事馆和警方报告外，继续进行广播工作。

最近，日本人故技重施。12月16日，XHA再次受到干扰，干扰声来自停泊在黄浦江上的一艘日本军舰。这是因为日本人企图控制上海的外资广播电台，要求这些电台将功率降至200瓦以下并申请注册。由于这一企图以失败告终，XHA成为第一个受到干扰的电台，其次是FFZ，随后该美国电台再次受到干扰。后一家电台的所有者明确表示，他绝不会投降。

很明显，日本人希望控制上海的外资广播电台，因为这些电台习惯于播报显然对日本不利的真实新闻。日本的举动为新闻评论员提供了最好的素材。日本人非但没有停止侵略行径，反而希望对广播电台实施控制。这只会为这些电台提供更多的新闻素材。

page_data.en:
December 21, 1940. Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News (comment) :-

"A STERN AND CLEAR STATEMENT"

In connection with the Japanese
interference with the broadcasting of the Hwa Mei Radio
Station, Mr. F.L. Healey, managing director of the radio
station, in the course of a statement yesterday, said "If
there's no change in a few days, you'll see some fun. The
United States has the most powerful equipment in the world.
We are going to give blow for blow so as to safeguard our
own interests and rights."
This stern and clear statement conveys
a feeling of joy to the listeners.
We understand that during these few
years the third party Powers have lost quite a fair amount
of their interests and rights in China because of
transgression. Heretofore the parties concerned have
adopted an attitude of conciliation and have never taken
any strong action to safeguard their own interests, with
the result that the other party has advanced further and
further. It is only recently that we have heard this
strong statement of dealing blow for blow. This is the
very statement that a third party nation, in her desire to
uphold her interests and rights, should have the courage
to make, because by means of this determination and
resolution not only will her own rights and interests be
safeguarded but the aggressiveness of the opponent will
thus be checked.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月21日。晨间译文

《中美日报》（评论）：-

“严厉而明确的声明”

关于日本干扰华美广播电台广播一事，该电台总经理F.L. Healey先生在昨日的一份声明中表示：“如果几天内没有变化，你们会看到好戏。美国拥有世界上最强大的设备。我们将以牙还牙，以捍卫我们自身的利益和权利。”

这一严厉而明确的声明让听众感到欣喜。

据了解，这几年第三方列强在中国因遭受侵犯而失去了相当多的利益和权利。此前，有关各方采取调和态度，从未采取有力行动维护自身利益，结果导致对方步步进逼。直到最近，我们才听到这种以牙还牙的强硬声明。这正是第三方国家为维护其利益和权利应有勇气做出的声明，因为凭借这种决心和意志，不仅能维护自身的权益，还能遏制对手的侵略气焰。

page_data.en:
Cheng, Yien Pao (brief comment) :-
"WIRELESS WAR" MAY OCCUR IN SHANGHAI
28/7/40
Frankly speaking, the so-called new order
which Japan has loudly advocated will never be able to
break through the old order of the United States for an
obvious reason, namely, the economic life of the so-called
new order of the Japanese lies within the scope of the old
order of the United States and this Japan can never break
through.
P. T. O.

Of late a dispute has arisen in Shanghai
because of the Japanese interference with the broadcasting
of an American radio station, and it is said that the
dispute may possibly give rise to a "wireless struggle".
We can very well expect that the final outcome of this
dispute will likewise be involved in the economic circle
mentioned above.
page_data.zh:
《诚言报》（简评）：-
上海可能发生“无线电战”
40年7月28日
坦率地说，日本大肆鼓吹的所谓“新秩序”永远无法突破美国的“旧秩序”，原因显而易见，即日本所谓“新秩序”的经济命脉处于美国“旧秩序”的范围之内，这是日本永远无法突破的。
请翻页

最近，由于日本干扰一家美国广播电台的广播，上海发生了一起争端，据说这场争端可能引发一场“无线电斗争”。我们可以很好地预期，这场争端的最终结果也将卷入上述经济圈子中。

page_data.en:
December 19, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Cheng Yien Pao :#

JAPANESE INTERFERENCE WITH BROADCASTING

XMHA, a local American radio station, is being interfered with by the Japanese.
According to information secured yesterday by our reporter, the broadcasts by this station showed an improvement yesterday afternoon because it had introduced certain mechanical means to deal with the interference by extending the wave length to 620 or 640. Thus, the Japanese interference will have no effect. It is learned that the station will change its K.C. from time to time as an act of resistance until the Japanese cease their interference.

On the morning of December 18, XMHA sent a written report to the American Consulate-General on the interference. The station is strongly opposed to Japanese action and says "Shanghai under the direction of the so-called 'new order' promoted by the Japanese is now in a state of anarchy as witness the interference with broadcasting stations and the disturbed conditions in the Western District."

A few days ago, the Japanese ceased interfering with F.F.Z, a French-owned radio station. As this station had refused to reduce its watts to 200, its broadcasts were interfered with again yesterday. It is learned that the station will make a report to the French Consulate-General with a request that negotiations be opened.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月19日。下午译文。

《诚言报》：#

日本干扰广播

本地美国广播电台XMHA正受到日本的干扰。
据本报记者昨日获得的消息，该电台的广播昨日下午有所改善，因为它引入了一些机械手段来应对干扰，将波长扩展至620或640。因此，日本的干扰将不起作用。据悉，作为抵抗行动，该电台将不时改变其千周数，直到日本停止干扰为止。

12月18日上午，XMHA就干扰事件向美国总领事馆提交了书面报告。该电台强烈反对日本的行动，并称“在日本推动的所谓‘新秩序’指导下，上海现在处于无政府状态，广播电台受到干扰以及西区局势动荡就是明证。”

几天前，日本停止了对法资广播电台F.F.Z.的干扰。由于该电台拒绝将其瓦特数降至200，其广播昨日再次受到干扰。据悉，该电台将向法国总领事馆提交报告，请求开启谈判。

page_data.en:
December 17, 1940.                                Afternoon Translation.

Cheng Yien Pao :-

"BROADCASTING OF FOREIGN OWNED RADIO STATION CONTINUOUSLY
INTERFERED WITH BY JAPANESE"

        X.M.H.A., the local American-owned radio
station, is a supporter of justice. For this reason, it
is hated by the Japanese.
        In a former issue of this paper, it was
reported that several weeks ago the Japanese Radio
Broadcasting Control authorities had decided to interfere
with the broadcast of this radio station. Yesterday, this
interference was started by the Japanese. Another radio
station that had been interfered with was X.M.H.D., the
Shanghai Christian Radio Station, but later it accepted
the demand of the Japanese to reduce its power to 200 watts,
with the result that it can now only be heard within only
100 miles of Shanghai. F.F.Z, the French Radio Station,
is still being interfered with.
        The object of the Japanese in interfering
with radio stations is to prevent Japanese people and the
people in the fallen areas from listening to outport news.
This deliberate interference with the legitimate rights
and interests of third nations is being condemned by various
foreign circles.
        It is learned that X.M.H.A. is preparing
various mechanical measures to overcome this interference
with its broadcasts by the Japanese.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月17日。                                下午译文。

《诚言报》：-

“外商拥有的广播电台广播持续受到日本人干扰”

        X.M.H.A.，这家本地美资广播电台，是正义的支持者。正因如此，它遭到日本人的憎恨。
        本报前几期曾报道，数周前，日本无线电广播管制当局已决定干扰该电台的广播。昨日，日本人开始了这种干扰。另一家受到干扰的电台是X.M.H.D.，即上海基督教广播电台，但后来它接受了日本人的要求，将功率降低至200瓦，结果现在只能在距离上海100英里范围内被收听到。F.F.Z.，即法国广播电台，仍在受到干扰。
        日本人干扰广播电台的目的是防止日本人和沦陷区民众收听外埠新闻。这种蓄意侵犯第三国合法权益的行为正受到各界外籍人士的谴责。
        据悉，X.M.H.A.正在准备各种技术措施，以克服日本人对其广播的干扰。

page_data.en:
Chinese-American Daily News (comment) :-
INTERFERENCE WITH AN AMERICAN RADIO STATION
The American radio station whose broadcasts
were much disturbed by Japanese in April last is again
being interfered with. This was first noticed at 4 p.m.
December 16. It is said that the interference comes from
a Japanese warship in the Whangpoo.
The Japanese are interfering with this
American radio station because it often broadcasts reports
and comments unfavourable to the Japanese.
Apart from creating a bad impression upon
foreigners, the Japanese can derive no benefit by this
interference with broadcasts.
page_data.zh:
《中美日报》（评论）：-
干扰美国广播电台
去年四月广播受到日本人严重干扰的那家美国广播电台，再次受到干扰。这一情况最早于12月16日下午4时被察觉。据说干扰来自黄浦江上的一艘日本军舰。
日本人干扰这家美国广播电台，是因为它经常播出不利于日本的报道和评论。
除了给外国人留下不良印象外，日本人通过这种广播干扰得不到任何好处。

page_data.en:
Cheng Yien Poo (comment) :-

INTERFERENCE WITH BROADCASTING OF FOREIGN STATIONS

According to information secured by this
paper, the Japanese are again interfering with broadcasting
by foreign radio stations. The broadcasting stations
affected are XHMA, a commercial station, XHMD, a Christian
station, and FFZ, a French station. If it is said that
the interference is being caused by the Chungking regime,
even the Japanese will have to admit that this is not so.
What is the cause of this interference
with foreign broadcasting? We cannot think of any cause.
It is up to the foreigners in Shanghai to frame a reply.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）
page_data.zh:
《诚言报》（评论）：-

干扰外国电台广播

据本报获得的消息，日本人再次干扰外国广播电台的广播。受影响的广播电台包括商业电台XHMA、基督教电台XHMD以及法国电台FFZ。如果说这种干扰是由重庆政权造成的，恐怕连日本人也不得不承认并非如此。
造成这种对外国广播干扰的原因是什么？我们想不出任何原因。这有待在上海的外国人作出回应。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科）

December 9, 40.

Commandant L. Fabre:
Directeur des Services de Police,
CONCESSION FRANÇAIS.

Dear Commandant:

With reference to your note of December
7, 1940, in regard to Station X.M.H.A., Race
Course Road, and an anti-Vichy Government broad-
cast, I agree with you entirely that a broadcast
of this nature is absolutely unnecessary in
Shanghai and can serve no useful purpose. I have
approached the Broadcasting Station, and have also
asked our Consul General to do anything he can to
assist. I have also referred the matter to Mr.
Phillips, the Secretary & Commissioner General, and
asked him to throw his weight into the balance.

Possibly we will get no satisfactory result,
but at least I can assure you that I will do every-
thing possible to stop or moderate this activity.

Yours sincerely:

L. Fabre 指挥官：

SECRET
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date December 9th 1940.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. B. REGISTRY
No S. B. D. 513/40(2)
261166 2 40

Subject French News Broadcast daily from Station X.M.H.A.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

At 4 p.m., December 6th, 1940 D.S.I. Logan,
acting on the instructions of the D.C. (Crime &
Special Branch) called on the manager of Radio
Station X.M.H.A. Mr. Healey (American) and informed
him that the Police considered the anti-Vichy
Government propaganda which is broadcast daily from
X.M.H.A., in the French language, prejudicial to
law and order and undesirable in the International
Settlement and requested him to discontinue
broadcasts of the nature indicated.

In reply, Mr. Healey stated that he could
not see his way clear to comply with the request
of the Police for the following reasons :-

X.M.H.A. is American owned and operated
and, according to the Constitution, there is no legal
restraint on free speech by Americans. Furthermore
the Station merely broadcasts Reuter and United
Press telegrams and also a reply to Transocean's
news bulletins which are broadcast daily from the
German radio station X.G.R.S., Great Western Road.
Moreover, the matter objected to which is broadcast
from X.M.H.A., is substantially the same as that
broadcast from the British station X.C.D.N. and the
broadcast is in fact done by the same people in
each case.

（左侧批注及印章）

秘密
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特务科第一股
报告
日期：1940年12月9日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
档案号 B. 登记处
编号 S. B. D. 513/40(2)
261166 2 40

主题：X.M.H.A.电台每日法语新闻广播。

由副督察长 Logan 制作，由督察长 Crawford 转呈

1940年12月6日下午4时，副督察长 Logan 奉刑事及特务科副处长的指示，拜访了X.M.H.A.广播电台经理 Healey 先生（美国人），并告知他，警方认为X.M.H.A.每日以法语播出的反维希政府宣传有害于治安，在国际租界内是不受欢迎的，并要求他停止播出上述性质的节目。

作为答复，Healey 先生表示，出于以下原因，他无法照办警方的要求：-

X.M.H.A. 为美国人所有并经营，根据宪法，美国人的言论自由不受法律限制。此外，该电台仅转播路透社和合众社的电讯，以及对每日从德国广播电台X.G.R.S.（大西路）广播的跨洋新闻公报的回应。而且，X.M.H.A.广播中受指责的内容，实质上与英国电台X.C.D.N.广播的内容相同，事实上在两种情况下均由同一批人进行广播。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. S. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 6813/14/XII(7)
9 / 2
December 7, 1946

Dear Major Bourne,

Station XMA, Race Course Road, is now
devoting itself to a campaign against a party of
our compatriots. Certain statements, which per-
haps the speakers do not fully realise, are of a
nature to provoke reactions.

You know, as I do, how inauspicious any
violent incidents between the French would be for
the maintenance of order in the International Settle-
ment. You will not fail to realise the disastrous
consequences of such incidents, in a city where
foreigners are watching us and who are ready to
exploit the least discord.

Quite frankly, I consider we should, at
all costs, unite in our efforts to restore peace
of mind, in such a way that everyone can continue
to do their duty, in a dignified manner, as is ex-
pedient in a country where we still have the chance
to work freely for the protection of French interests.

Without wishing to ask you to take any
strong action which would be contrary to our policy,
I should very much appreciate if you would use your
influence to draw the attention of the proprietors of
Station XMA to the fact that, without in the least
wishing to we are sure, they are making themselves
partisans of an agitation very detrimental to the interests
and even to the existence of the entire foreign community.

Thanking you ,
Yours sincerely,
(Signed) L. Pira

1946年12月7日 [注：原文年份疑似笔误，结合上下文应为1940年]

亲爱的 Bourne 少校：

跑马厅路的XMA电台目前正致力于开展针对我们要部分同胞的运动。某些言论，或许演讲者并未充分意识到其性质，可能会引发反应。

您和我一样清楚，法国人之间的任何暴力事件对于维持国际租界的秩序都是多么不利。您不会不考虑到，在一个外国人注视着我们、并准备利用哪怕最微小分歧的城市里，此类事件会带来灾难性的后果。

坦率地说，我认为我们应该不惜一切代价团结努力，恢复人心安定，以便每个人都能继续以得体的方式履行自己的职责，这在一个我们仍有幸能自由工作以保护法国利益的国家里是适宜的。

我并不希望要求您采取任何违背我们政策的强硬行动，但如果您能运用您的影响力，提请XMA电台业主注意这样一个事实，我们将不胜感激：虽然我们相信他们绝非有意，但他们正成为一场非常不利于整个外籍社群利益甚至生存的煽动活动的帮凶。

谢谢，
此致
敬礼，
（签名）L. Pira

X M H A

October 10, 1940.

Mr. R.W. Yorke,
Assistant Commissioner, S.M.P.
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Yorke:

In my 8 a.m. broadcast on Monday, I read
the report appearing in the China Press on Page 2
regarding the notice published in the Shanghai Zaria
by the Ivanoff Russian Emigres' Committee warning
Russians not to patronize the Russian Daily News.

In signing off, I adlibbed the thought that the
notice smacked of intimidation of the sort that has
taken place in Harbin, Mukden and other cities of the north.

I also remarked that Ivanoff apparently was following
the lines of least resistance which, according to all
information on the subject, was contrary to the policy
that had been assumed by the late Charles Metzler.
I also said that this new policy of the Emigres'
Committee would only hold the name of Metzler in greater
esteem hereabouts.

There was nothing more said. This is pure editorial
comment and in view of the notice in the Shanghai Zaria
as reported by the China Press, perfectly justified.
I am quite willing to repeat it at any time. I would like
to point out that I will not submit to any intimidation
of myself by the committee which Ivanoff heads.

Sincerely,

(Sd.) C.D. Alcott

Certified true copy

X M H A

1940年10月10日。

R.W. Yorke 先生，
上海公共租界工部局警务处助理处长，
上海。

亲爱的 Yorke 先生：

在我周一上午8时的广播中，我宣读了《字林西报》第2页刊登的一则报道，内容是关于伊万诺夫俄侨委员会在《上海柴拉报》上发布的通告，警告俄国人不要光顾《俄罗斯日报》。

在结束广播时，我即兴发挥，认为该通告带有哈尔滨、沈阳及其他北方城市曾发生的那种恐吓意味。

我还评论说，伊万诺夫显然是在遵循阻力最小的路线，根据关于此事的所有信息，这与已故 Charles Metzler 所采取的政策背道而驰。我还说，俄侨委员会的这一新政策只会让此地的人们更加尊敬 Metzler 的名字。

没有再说其他内容。这是纯粹的编辑评论，鉴于《字林西报》报道的《上海柴拉报》上的通告，这是完全正当的。我随时愿意重复这一观点。我想指出，我不会屈服于伊万诺夫领导的委员会对我的任何恐吓。

此致，

（签署）C.D. Alcott

认证副本属实

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
Oct 7 1940

Committee Warns Russians To
Blacklist Pro-Soviet Daily

In the first direct order to the
Russian community here since the
murder of Charles E. Metzler lift-
ed Nicolai E. Ivanow to head the
Russian Emigrants' Committee, the
latter administrative body yester-
day warned all Russian emigres to
abstain from dealings of any sort
with the pro-Soviet Russian Daily
News—or be regarded as helpers
of the "enemy."

A notification placed in the
"White" Shanghai Zaria "advised"
all Russian emigre concerns and
individuals to sever immediately all
relations with the blacklisted news-
paper, and to withhold from it all
announcements and advertisements.
Officials of the Russian Daily News
yesterday stated they would not
let this move against them pass
unnoticed.

Charging the daily with agitating
among emigres against the Nanking
authorities, the Committee declared
that the journal "does not even stop
before provocative statements. In
number 266 of this newspaper there
appeared a mythical interview with
the Commissioner of the Settlement
police," the notification hinted.

This allusion, it was believed, dealt
with the stand taken by the
Shanghai Municipal Police on
Mayor Fu Siao-en's decree that all
Russian emigres be henceforward
tried in the Nantao Court of the
City Government of Greater Shang-
hai. Major Kenneth M. Bourne,
S.M.P. Commissioner, told THE
CHINA PRESS that the force he
headed would continue bringing
arrested Russians for trial in the
First Special District Court, and this
statement later appeared in the
Russian Daily News.

"Let emigres not forget for a
single minute," the Committee
warned, "that by these actions the
Russian Daily News plainly showed
that it is the political enemy of
Russian emigres, and that conse-
quently all those who in one way or
another contribute to its success and
material welfare will be regarded as
elements aiding an enemy organ."
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1940年10月7日

委员会警告俄国人
将亲苏日报列入黑名单

自 Charles E. Metzler 遇刺身亡、Nicolai E. Ivanow 被推举为俄国侨民委员会主席以来，该行政机构昨日向在沪俄国社区发出了第一道直接命令，警告所有俄国侨民 abstain from dealings of any sort with the pro-Soviet Russian Daily News（ refrain from any dealings with the pro-Soviet *Russian Daily News* / 避免与亲苏的《俄罗斯日报》进行任何形式的往来）——否则将被视为“敌人”的帮凶。

一份刊登在“白俄”报纸《上海霞报》（Shanghai Zaria）上的通知“建议”所有俄国侨民企业和个人立即切断与被列黑名单的这家报纸的一切关系，并停止向其发布任何公告和广告。《俄罗斯日报》的官员昨日表示，他们不会让这一针对他们的举动轻易过去。

委员会指责该日报在侨民中煽动反对南京当局的情绪，并宣称该刊物“甚至不惜发表挑衅性言论”。通知暗示，“在该报第266期中，出现了一篇与租界警务总监进行的虚构访谈。”

据信，这一影射涉及上海公共租界工部局警务处对上海市大上海市政府市长傅筱庵法令所持的立场，该法令规定此后所有俄国侨民均由上海市政府南市法院审理。上海公共租界工部局警务处总监 Kenneth M. Bourne 少校告诉《字林西报》，他所领导的警队将继续把被捕的俄国人送往第一特区法院受审，这一声明随后出现在《俄罗斯日报》上。

委员会警告说：“让侨民们一刻也不要忘记，《俄罗斯日报》通过这些行动清楚地表明，它是俄国侨民的政治敌人，因此，所有以某种方式为其成功和物质福利做出贡献的人，都将被视为协助敌对机构的分子。”

page_data.en:
OCT 8 1940
OFF THE RECORD
White Hopes
"White" Russians here comfort themselves with
the thought that should the Japanese take over
Shanghai good and proper they'll all be given Soviet
papers. Except, of course, those who could not love
Russia so much did they not love the New Order
more.
Many say they had it on good authority
that the "Reds" are willing to forgive and for-
get. With Japanese sentries ruling the roost
in Tientsin, most emigres there have been
granted Soviet papers, they say. It is reported
that during the floods in that port the Soviet
Consulate doled out food and shelter to the
emigres—and even put a notification to that
effect in the Nippon-fearing "Nasha Zaria,"
sister journal of the Shanghai Zaria that
printed Ivanow's ukas blacklisting the pro-So-
viet Russian Daily News.
Ivanow, they say, is in a "white" rage over the
beating he took at the rhetoric of Carroll Alcott.
The newscaster called his step in warning emigres
from having anything to do with the Daily News as
"the meanest and most cussed example of intimida-
tion I have come across in a long time." Mr. Alcott
declared that the step only served to elevate the
name of the late Charles E. Metzler, whose assassina-
tion put Ivanow at the head of the Russian Emigrants
Committee. "You can judge for yourself what that
does to the name of Ivanow," Mr. Alcott said.
page_data.zh:
1940年10月8日
非正式记录
白俄的希望

在沪“白俄”以这样一种想法自我安慰：如果日本人彻底接管上海，他们都将获得苏联证件。当然，除了那些若非更爱“新秩序”就不会如此热爱俄罗斯的人之外。

许多人称，他们有可靠消息来源指出，“红军”愿意宽恕并忘却前嫌。他们说，随着日本哨兵在天津占据主导地位，那里的大多数侨民已获得苏联证件。据报道，在该港口发生洪水期间，苏联领事馆向侨民分发食物并提供住所——甚至还在惧怕日本的《我们的霞报》（Nasha Zaria）上刊登了此类通知，该报是上海《霞报》的姊妹刊，而上海《霞报》曾刊登 Ivanow 将亲苏的《俄罗斯日报》列入黑名单的指令。

据说，Ivanow 因在 Carroll Alcott 的言辞攻击下受挫而处于“白”色愤怒之中。这位广播员称，Ivanow 警告侨民不要与《俄罗斯日报》有任何往来的举动是“我许久以来所见过的最卑鄙、最可恶的恐吓例子”。Alcott 先生宣称，这一举动只会提升已故 Charles E. Metzler 的名声，正是 Metzler 的遇刺使 Ivanow 登上了俄国侨民委员会主席之位。“你可以自己判断这对 Ivanow 的名声有何影响，” Alcott 先生说。

page_data.en:
Mr. Carroll Alcott
Attacked by Paper

Radio Speaker's Comment
Slammed by Russian Daily;
Russian Papers' War

The recent order, issued by Mr.
N. A. Ivanow, new head of the
Russian Emigrants' Committee, for-
bidding Russian emigres to buy and
advertise in the "Russian Daily
News," started quite a little war
between the above daily and Russian
emigrant newspapers, where editori-
als aimed at each other have been
printed for several days. The affair
reached a different angle yesterday
when a Russian daily attacked Mr.
Carroll Alcott for not "minding his
own business" when he commented
upon the order in his radio broadcast
on Monday evening.

According to the paper, Mr. Alcott
said that the Russians should judge
for themselves what they are to do
and that it was not Mr. Ivanow's
business to mix into the Russian
public's private affairs. The paper
also stated that, since Mr. Alcott is
an American, it was his business
still less to comment upon the order.
It was also reported that Mr. Ivanow
would file a protest with the Shang-
hai Municipal Council against the
attack directed by Mr. Alcott in his
recent broadcast.

Helpers of the "Enemy"

The order, which started quite a
storm in the Russian newspaper
columns, was given in the "Shanghai
Zaria" a few days ago when Mr.
Ivanow warned the Russian Com-
munity against dealing with the pro-
Soviet daily and that those who con-
tinued to do so would be regarded
as helpers of the "enemy." The
"Russian Daily News" was charged
with agitating among Russians against
the Nanking Government and printing
provocative statements.

A stronger attack was launched
against the pro-Soviet paper by the
"Far Eastern Times," Russian-lan-
guage paper sponsored by the Japa-
nese, which stated in its editorial
that unless the "Russian Daily News"
stopped printing derogatory state-
ments against the Nanking Govern-
ment and the actions of the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, it would be
closed.

It will be remembered that the
"Russian Daily News" was bombed
last year when a missile was thrown
into its offices. Lately, Mr. V.
Chilikin, editor of the paper, was
warned that he would meet a
similar end to that suffered by Sub-
Inspector P. M. Yankovsky who,
according to reliable sources, was
murdered because he knew too
much.

Carroll Alcott 先生
遭报纸攻击

电台播音员的评论
遭《俄罗斯日报》抨击；
俄文报纸间的战争

俄国侨民委员会新任主席 N. A. Ivanow 先生最近发布的命令，禁止俄国侨民购买《俄罗斯日报》或在该报刊登广告，引发了上述日报与俄国侨民报纸之间的一场小战争，双方社论相互攻讦已持续数日。昨日，事态出现了新的角度，一家俄文日报攻击 Carroll Alcott 先生，称他在周一晚间的广播中评论该命令是“多管闲事”。

据该报称，Alcott 先生说俄国人应自行判断该如何做，干涉俄国公众的私人事务并非 Ivanow 先生的分内之事。该报还指出，既然 Alcott 先生是美国人，他评论该命令更是越俎代庖。另有报道称，Ivanow 先生将就 Alcott 先生在近期广播中发起的攻击向上海公共租界工部局提出抗议。

“敌人”的帮凶

这项在俄文报纸专栏中掀起轩然大波的命令，几天前发表在《上海霞报》上，当时 Ivanow 先生警告俄国社区不要与这家亲苏日报打交道，并称继续这样做的人将被视为“敌人”的帮凶。《俄罗斯日报》被指控在俄国人中煽动反对南京政府的情绪，并刊登挑衅性言论。

由日本人资助的俄文报纸《远东时报》（Far Eastern Times）对这家亲苏报纸发起了更猛烈的攻击，其社论称，除非《俄罗斯日报》停止刊登针对南京政府和俄国侨民委员会行动的贬损性言论，否则将被查封。

人们还记得，《俄罗斯日报》去年曾遭轰炸，一枚投掷物被扔进其办公室。最近，该报编辑 V. Chilikin 先生受到警告，称他将遭遇与副督察 P. M. Yankovsky 类似的结局，据可靠消息来源称，Yankovsky 因知道得太多而被谋杀。

Mr. R.W. Yorke,
Assistant Commissioner, S.M.P.
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Yorke:

In my 8 a.m. broadcast on Monday, I read
the report appearing in the China Press on Page 2
regarding the notice published in the Shanghai Zaria
by the Ivanoff Russian Emigres' Committee warning
Russians not to patronize the Russian Daily News.

In signing off, I ad libbed the thought that the
notice smacked of intimidation of the sort that has
taken place in Farbin, Mukden and other cities of
the north.

I also remarked that Ivanoff apparently was following
the lines of least resistance which, according to all
information on the subject, was contrary to the policy
that had been assumed by the late Charles Metzler.
I also said that this new policy of the Emigres'
Committee would only the name of Metzler in greater
esteem hereabouts. (Hold

There was nothing more said. This is pure editorial
comment and in view of the notice in the Shanghai Zaria
as reported by the China Press, perfectly justified.
I am quite willing to repeat it at any time. I would like
to point out that I will not submit to any intimidation
of myself by the committee which Ivanoff heads.

Sincerely,
C.D.Alcott

Lane 118, Moulmein Road,
Shanghai, 7th October 1940.

G. G. Phillips, Esq.,
Secretary & Commissioner General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have the honour to draw your kind attention to the
broadcasting made by the Radio Station X.M.H.A., 445 Race Course
Road, at 8 o'clock a.m. to-day, in which broadcasting there was
a propaganda directed against Mr. Fu Siao Yen, Mayor of the Spe-
cial City Government of Shanghai, my Committee and myself.

As I know, Municipal Authorities of the International
Settlement never allow any political propaganda within its territory,
and, therefore, I beg to request you to take necessary steps to
cease any propaganda by the said station directed against Rus-
sian Emigrants' Colony here in general and my Committee in par-
ticular.

I may only wonder why Russian Emigrants' Colony so inte-
rests said Station and it would be much better if the station
forgets for ever about our existence.

Awaiting your answer.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(Signed) N.A. Ivanow,
Acting Chairman.

据本人所知，国际租界市政当局从不允许在其领土内进行任何政治宣传，因此，本人恳请阁下采取必要措施，制止该电台针对此处俄国侨民群体，特别是针对本人委员会的任何宣传。

等候阁下的答复。

Sir,

    I beg to report that on 6/9/40, I was detailed on night
duty at the back entrance of Radio Station X.M.H.A., at Lane
429 Chungking Road together with C.P.C. 667.
    At 17.35 a.m. 7/9/40, I saw a black painted hire car being
driven into the lane, in which was seated four persons, presumab-
ly Japanese. When the car was stopped outside the back door
of the radio station, three persons alighted from same; one of
them asked us in Chinese "where is No. 18" to which we answered
"we don't know." Thereupon one of them, wearing black foreign
style clothing, produced a pistol. This man seized hold of my
left hand and another one seized hold of the right hand of
C.P.C. 667. They ordered us to get into the waiting car. We
complied but when we were nearing the car, we broke away and
ran towards the entrance to the lane. The three persons ran
after us but when we reached the entrance to the lane, we
looked back and found the three persons were not chasing us
any more. We then came to the station to report.

    The above statement is true.

                                Signed:- Zau Vung Han.
                                         C.P.C. 774.

    1940年9月7日凌晨0时35分，我看见一辆漆成黑色的租赁汽车驶入弄堂，车内坐着四个人，推测为日本人。当该车停在上述广播电台后门外面时，三人下车；其中一人用中文问我们“18号在哪里？”，我们回答“不知道”。随即，其中一名身穿黑色西式服装的人掏出手枪。此人抓住我的右手，另一人抓住中国巡捕774号的左手。他们命令我们进入等候的汽车。我们照做了，但在靠近汽车时，我们挣脱开来，向弄堂入口跑去。那三人追赶我们，但当我们到达弄堂入口时，回头发现那三人不再追赶。随后我们来到警局报告。在奔跑过程中，我遗失了执勤帽。
    以上是我的真实陈述。

                        签名:- Lee Soong Liem.

Anonymous letter implying threats received per postal delivery by
Mr. Alcott, X.M.H.A. Radio Station News Commentator
D. I. Hill
Officer i/c.

DC (S/Branch)
Sir
Information
Office

Sir,

I beg to report that Mr. Carroll D. Alcott, U.S.
citizen, Radio News Commentator for X.M.H.A. Radio
Station, No. 445 Race Course Road, received per postal
delivery on the 23-8-40, an anonymous letter implying
threats, the letter which is purported to have been
sent by a Russian female is typewritten on plain paper
and reads as follows:-

August 22, 1940.

Mr. Carol Alcott,
c/o XMHA Broadcasting Stn.,
445 Race Course Road,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Mr. Alcott,

As a Russian girl I shouldn't be
much concerned about your safety, your remarks
about emigrant Russians in general and Russian
girls in particular being usually far from flatter-
ing; still, as a partisan of the same political
opinions, I wish you will and, therefore, want to
draw your attention to the rumours spreading around
town and originating, as far as I could ascertain,
North of the Creek, to the effect that, in case you
decide to leave town, you will not be allowed to do
so alive.

Of course, you know how to take care
of yourself, but just in case you really decide to
take up travelling as a recreation and overlook the
advisability of travelling on a U. S. man-of-war, I
would suggest that you not only endeavour to do so,
but that you embark straight from a Navy car together
with some of your Navy friends.

Just to let me know that you received
this, perhaps altogether superfluous, message, do
mention same in one of your 7-30 a.m. broadcasts, so
that I may be sure not to miss it.

With best wishes,

Nina T.

was sent by some person connected with the "Soviet News

1940年8月22日。

卡罗尔·阿尔科特先生，
转交 XMHA 广播电台，
跑马厅路445号，

亲爱的阿尔科特先生：

作为一名俄罗斯女孩，我本不应太关心您的安全，因为您对一般俄罗斯移民，特别是俄罗斯女孩的评论通常远非恭维；然而，作为持有相同政治观点的支持者，我希望您能平安，因此想提请您注意在市面流传的谣言，据我所知，这些谣言起源于苏州河北岸，大意是，如果您决定离开本市，您将不被允许活着离开。

为了让我知道您收到了这封或许完全多余的信息，请在您早上7:30的广播节目中提及此事，以便我确信不会错过。

致以最美好的祝愿，

尼娜·T.

Sir,
At 7.45 p.m. 2-8-40 F.P.S. 150 Nyberg on duty at Radio Station X.M.H.A. 445 Race Course Road telephoned to the station to report that Mr. Alcott had received another telephone threat.
The undersigned attended and interviewed Mr. Alcott when the following was learned.
At 7.10 p.m. 2-8-40 the telephone rang at Radio Station X.M.H.A. and was answered by Mr. Vic. Schmierson, Sports Reporter. The caller asked to speak to Mr. Alcott. Mr. Alcott then answered the phone, telling the caller that Mr. Alcott was not in, but that he could take any message for Mr. Alcott. The caller then said "Tell Mr. Alcott that he must go" he then slammed down the receiver. Mr. Alcott states that judging, from the man's accent, he believes that the caller was a Japanese.
（批：R.W.Y.）
Mr. Frank Moss, X.M.H.A. station announcer reported to the undersigned that at about 12 m.n. 1-8-40, when he left the radio station for his home, he saw a silver coloured, two seater, sports model motor-car parked across the street from the radio station facing East on Race Course Road. As the car appeared very much like one owned by Mr. Don. Chisholm, Mr. Moss thought it was Mr. Chisholm sitting at the driving seat. He shouted "Hello Don" but receiving no answer, Mr. Moss started to cross the street to talk to the man he thought was Mr. Chisholm. However, the car started up and was speedily driven East on Race Course Road and had reached the intersection of

本人到场并采访了阿尔科特先生，获悉以下情况。
1940年8月2日晚上7时10分，X.M.H.A.广播电台的电话响起，由体育记者维克·施米尔森（Vic. Schmierson）先生接听。来电者要求与阿尔科特先生通话。阿尔科特先生随后接起电话，告诉来电者阿尔科特先生不在，但他可以代为留言。来电者随后说：“告诉阿尔科特先生，他必须走人”，然后挂断了电话。阿尔科特先生表示，根据那人的口音判断，他认为来电者是日本人。
（批注：R.W.Y.）
X.M.H.A.电台播音员弗兰克·莫斯（Frank Moss）先生向本人报告，1940年8月1日午夜12时左右，当他离开广播电台回家时，看见一辆银色的双座运动型汽车停在广播电台对面的街道上，车头朝东停在跑马厅路上。由于这辆车看起来非常像唐·奇泽姆（Don. Chisholm）先生拥有的一辆车，莫斯先生以为坐在驾驶座上的是奇泽姆先生。他喊道“你好，唐”，但没有得到回应，莫斯先生便开始穿过街道，想与他以为是奇泽姆先生的人交谈。然而，汽车启动并迅速沿跑马厅路向东驶去，在

Mohawk Road before Mr. Moss had crossed the street. As
it was dark, and the car travelled so fast, Mr. Moss was
unable to note the licence number.

Mr. Moss states that he is on friendly terms with
Mr. Chisholm and is sure that if it was latter's car Mr.
Chisholm would have replied to his friendly hail. He now
believes it was some other person watching the station,
who did not wish to be recognised, when Mr. Moss started
to cross the street, and so drove away.

C.P.C. 3024 on duty in front of the radio station

I beg to report, that at 7.45 p.m. 31/7/49, the
undersigned on request proceeded to "X H X A" Radio
Station, No. 445 Race Course Road and there interviewed

"I have received information from Major Williams,
U.S. Naval Attaché and Mr. Richard P. Butrick United
States Consul General, to the effect that the former
mentioned are in possession of certain information
allegedly received from Japanese Naval Sources to the
effect that a possible attempt will be made in the very
near future to assassinate one or two of the list of
foreigners recently ordered for deportation from
Shanghai by the "Wang Ching Wei" Government. I have
been given to understand that a possible attempt will
be made on my life, this may mean that the "Wang Ching
Wei" Government would attempt to force the "Powers" to
recognise them by whatever diplomatic negotiations may
be subsequently instituted. I have been advised by
the U.S. Consul General Mr. Butrick, to take extreme
precautions. I therefore have decided to take up
residence by day between the hours of 7 a.m. and 11 p.m.
at the Radio Station No. 445 Race Course Road, and at
night between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. at my present address
No. 147 Rue Paul Henry Apt. 11. Tele. 78531. I there-

Confidential
Misc. 232/40.
Chengtu Road
July 30th, 40.
Threats received by telephone at Radio Station X. M. H. A. 445 Race
Course Road against Mr. C. D. Alcott's news broadcasts.
D. S. Taylor,
（批：DC (Grand) / Sir / Information / Acc / D.S.）
Sir,
At 8.30 a.m. 30-7-40, F.P.S. 150 Nyberg reported to
the Officer i/c that Mr. Carroll Alcott had informed him
that at 10.20 p.m. 29-7-40 a telephone message had been
received at Radio Station X.M.H.A, 445 Race Course Road
warning that Mr. Alcott's news broadcasts should be dis-
continued within three days.
The undersigned interviewed Mr. Alcott and also Mr.
Frank Ross, X.M.H.A. station announcer, who had received
the telephone call and, as a result, the following details
were obtained.
At 10.15 p.m. 29-7-40, Mr. Alcott commenced his usual
evening news broadcast over Radio Station X.M.H.A. 445
Race Course Road. At 10.20 p.m. 29-7-40 the telephone rang
at the radio station and Mr. Frank Ross answered. The
following conversation in English then ensued.
Caller: "Take that shit off the air. I give him three
days to get off the air. See!!"
Mr. Ross: "What did you say ?"
Caller: "You heard me. I said take that shit off the
air."
Mr. Ross: "Sounds screwy to me."
Caller: "Nothing screwy about it. I give him three
days to get off the air."
Mr. Ross: "Why dont you tell that to Mr. Alcott
himself ?"
Caller: "Alright I will. What time does his broad-
cast finish ?"
Mr. Ross: "About 10.35 p.m. Who is that speaking ?"
Caller: "Fong" "You heard me, speak with a V.
I give him three days to get off the
Air !"
（批：5' / (- ½ / (A) ）

机密
杂项 232/40。
成都路
1940年7月30日。
位于跑马厅路445号的X.M.H.A.广播电台收到针对C. D. Alcott先生新闻广播的电话威胁。
D. S. Taylor，
（批注：DC (Grand) / 阁下 / 知悉 / Acc / D.S.）
阁下，
1940年7月30日上午8时30分，巡捕房第150号警员Nyberg向负责警官报告称，Carroll Alcott先生告知他，1940年7月29日晚上10时20分，位于跑马厅路445号的X.M.H.A.广播电台接到一通电话，警告Alcott先生的新闻广播必须在三天内停止。
签署人面谈了Alcott先生以及X.M.H.A.电台播音员Frank Ross先生，后者接听了该电话，由此获得以下细节。
1940年7月29日晚上10时15分，Alcott先生开始在跑马厅路445号的X.M.H.A.广播电台进行惯常的晚间新闻广播。1940年7月29日晚上10时20分，广播电台的电话响起，Frank Ross先生接听。随后发生了如下英语对话。
来电者：“把那堆屎从空中撤下来。我给他三天时间停播。听见没！！”
Ross先生：“你说什么？”
来电者：“你听见了。我说把那堆屎从空中撤下来。”
Ross先生：“我觉得这听起来有点疯。”
来电者：“一点也不疯。我给他三天时间停播。”
Ross先生：“你为什么不直接告诉Alcott先生本人？”
来电者：“好吧，我会的。他的广播什么时候结束？”
Ross先生：“大约晚上10点35分。你是谁？”
来电者：“Fong” “你听见了，说话带V音。
我给他三天时间停
播！”
（批注：5' / (- ½ / (A) ）

page_data.en:
- 2 -
Mr. Moss states that in the middle of the conversation he had recognised the voice of the caller, but had prolonged the conversation to make sure. He states that he is quite sure that the caller was a Russian Jew, of his acquaintance, named Nathaniel Rabin alias Rabinovitch, who is known to have connections with the Japanese Authorities and is now said to be connected with the Special Service Corps of the Japanese Army. Mr. Moss states that he had known Rabin for a period of about 5 years, and he is quite certain that it was this man's voice he heard over the telephone.

After Mr. Alcott had finished his broadcast Mr. Moss informed him of the telephone call and also told Mr. Alcott that he was convinced that the caller was a man named Rabin.

At 1.30 a.m. 30-7-40, Mr. Alcott was awakened by the telephone ringing in his home. He got up and answered the phone whereupon the caller, obviously a foreigner speaking with a slight Russian accent, told Mr. Alcott that he had just three days in which to discontinue his news broadcasts. Mr. Alcott asked the man why he did not come and give his message direct to Mr. Alcott's face instead of calling on the telephone and, acting on the information given by Mr. Moss, addressed the caller as Rabin. The caller, apparently caught off guard, asked how Mr. Alcott knew his name, and then said it made no difference and repeated that Mr. Alcott had only three days to get off the air. He then slammed down the receiver.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
Moss先生陈述，在谈话中途他已认出来电者的声音，但为了确认起见延长了通话时间。他陈述，他十分确定来电者是他认识的一名俄籍犹太人，名叫Nathaniel Rabin，又名Rabinovitch，此人据知与日本当局有联系，且目前据说与日本陆军特务机关有关联。Moss先生陈述，他认识Rabin约5年，他非常肯定他在电话里听到的是此人的声音。

Alcott先生结束广播后，Moss先生告知了他这通电话的情况，并告诉Alcott先生，他确信来电者是一个名叫Rabin的人。

1940年7月30日凌晨1时30分，Alcott先生被家中的电话铃声吵醒。他起身接听电话，来电者显然是一名外国人，说话带有轻微的俄罗斯口音，他告诉Alcott先生，他只有三天时间停止新闻广播。Alcott先生问此人为什么不直接当面传达信息，而是打电话，并根据Moss先生提供的信息，称呼来电者为Rabin。来电者显然措手不及，问Alcott先生怎么知道他的名字，然后说这无关紧要，并重申Alcott先生只有三天时间停播。随后他挂断了电话。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

In view of the certainty of Mr. Moss regarding his
recognition of the caller's voice and the subsequent
tacit admission of his identity as Rabin, when Mr. Alcott
addressed him by this name, there seems to be good reason
to believe that the caller was in fact Nathaniel Rabin
alias Rabirovitch.

This man was formerly a musician, playing in local
cabarets and at one time, a few years ago, managed the
Little Club on Bubbling Well Road. During the period of
Sino-Japanese hostilities in the Shanghai area, Rabin
used his connections with the Japanese authorities to
obtain permits for the removal of cargoes, belonging to
Chinese, from restricted areas. It is said that he is
now actively connected with the Japanese Army Special
Service Section.

There are two C.P.C.'s constantly on guard at the
rear of the premises of Radio Station X.M.H.A. while
another C.P.C. is on duty at the front of the premises.
In addition to the above P.P.S. 180 Egeberg is on duty
daily at the radio station during all news broadcasts
i.e. 7.50 a.m., 1 p.m., and 10.15 p.m. When asked if he
wished any further precautionary measures to be taken for
his protection Mr. Alcott stated that, if possible, he
would like to have a Foreign Police escort throughout
the day - commencing from 7 a.m. until about 11 p.m. - to
accompany him to and from his home, to his office and the
radio station, there being periods during the day when
the escort would not be required.

- 3 -

鉴于Moss先生对认出来电者声音的确定性，以及当Alcott先生以此名称呼来电者时，对方默许了其身份为Rabin，我们有充分理由相信来电者确系Nathaniel Rabin，又名Rabirovitch。

此人曾是一名音乐家，在当地歌舞厅演奏，并在几年前一度管理静安寺路的Little Club。在上海地区中日敌对行动期间，Rabin利用其与日本当局的关系，获取许可证，将属于中国人的货物从限制区运出。据说他目前与日本陆军特务部积极勾结。

X.M.H.A.广播电台 premises 后方始终有两名中国巡捕（C.P.C.）守卫，另有一名中国巡捕在 premises 前方执勤。除上述人员外，第180号外籍巡捕Egeberg在所有新闻广播期间（即上午7时50分、下午1时和晚上10时15分）每日在该电台执勤。当被问及是否希望采取进一步的预防措施以保护其安全时，Alcott先生表示，如果可能的话，他希望全天——从上午7时至晚上11时左右——由一名外籍警察护送，陪同他往返于住所、办公室和广播电台之间，因为在一天中的某些时段并不需要护送。

1.

Threat to Carroll B. Alcott, X.M.H.A.
Radio Announcer.

Mr. Carroll B. Alcott, U.S. Citizen, Radio
Announcer at X.M.H.A. Radio Station, 445 Race Course
Road, against whom threats have recently been made,
received further threats yesterday, 29-7-40, and again
today, 30-7-40.

At 10.20p.m. 29-7-40, Mr. Frank Moss, announcer at
445 Race Course Road, received a telephone message from
a male whose voice he recognised as being that of one
NATHANIEL RABIN, Russian Jew. Rabin requested that Mr.
Alcott be told that "he had just three days in which to
get off the air." Mr. Moss is personally acquainted
with Rabin and is certain that it was his voice that
gave the above message.

At 1.20a.m. 30-7-40, Mr. Alcott who was at his
home at 187 Route Paul Henri was awakened by a telephone
call; a male voice repeating a similar message to that
which Mr. Moss had received. Mr. Alcott in reply
addressed the caller as "Rabin" whereupon the latter
asked him how it was that he knew his name. Mr. Alcott
answered that he recognised his voice, whereupon Rabin
said: "What difference does it make who I am. You have
three days in which to get off the air." Rabin then rang
off.

1.

对X.M.H.A.
电台播音员Carroll B. Alcott的威胁。

美国公民Carroll B. Alcott先生，系跑马厅路445号X.M.H.A.广播电台播音员，近期受到威胁，昨日（1940年7月29日）及今日（1940年7月30日）再次受到威胁。

1940年7月29日晚上10时20分，跑马厅路445号播音员Frank Moss先生接到一名男子的电话，他认出该声音属于NATHANIEL RABIN，一名俄籍犹太人。Rabin要求转告Alcott先生，“他只有三天时间停播。” Moss先生与Rabin私交相识，并确信上述信息是由Rabin的声音传达的。

1940年7月30日凌晨1时20分，住在亨利路187号的Alcott先生被电话叫醒；一个男声重复了Moss先生收到的类似信息。Alcott先生在回复中称呼来电者为“Rabin”，后者随即问他如何知道他的名字。Alcott先生回答说他听出了他的声音，于是Rabin说：“我是谁有什么关系。你有三天时间停播。” Rabin随后挂断电话。

page_data.en:
1/2.

Mr. Alcott, a copy of whose letter reporting the
matter to the U.S. Consul General is hereto attached,
states that he knows Rubin by sight but that he is not
personally acquainted with him. He further states that
he believes him to be in the employ of the Special
Service Section of the Japanese Army.

In connection with Mr. Alcott's reference to
Rubin's predilection for the North side of the Soochow
Creek it is to be noted that one "H. Robbins" is listed
among the residents of Broadway Mansions.

Mr. Alcott stated that his reasons for reporting the
affair to the police was to make certain that it was
placed on record.

关于Alcott先生提及Rubin偏爱苏州河北岸一事，需注意百老汇大厦的居民名单中列有一名“H. Robbins”。

Alcott先生陈述，他向警方报告此事的原因是为了确保此事留有记录。

July 30, 1940.

Mr. R.P. Butrick,
U.S. Consul-General,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Mr. Butrick;

I would like to report another threat made against me last night. It came from a foreigner whom I have good reason to believe is in the employ of the Special Service Section of the Japanese Army, a man named Nathaniel Rabin, believed to be a Russian Jew from Harbin although he has attempted to pass himself off as an American.

Rabin called Radio Station XNHA at 10.30p.m. yesterday, July 29. The announcer on duty, Mr. Frank Moss, took the call. Rabin, who refused to give his name, told the announcer to tell me that I had just three days in which to get off the air.

Moss gave me this information, at the same time announcing that he knew who the man was who had called. He said it was Nathaniel Rabin whom he knew personally. He recognized his voice, he stated, and would swear to it that it was Rabin. Moss informed me that he had asked Rabin why he didn't call me personally and deliver the message.

About 1.20a.m. this morning, I was awakened from my sleep at my home by a telephone call. A foreigner's voice repeated the message that had been given to Moss, namely that I had three days in which to get off the air. Acting on the tip given me by Mr. Moss, I addressed the caller as Rabin. He asked me how I knew his name and I told him that I recognized his voice. He then said; "What difference does it make who I am. You have three days in which to get off the air." He then slammed down the receiver.

I have already reported the threat to the Police and I thought it best to inform you at the same time.

In view of the statement made by Moss that he
page_data.zh:
1940年7月30日。

R.P. Butrick先生，
美国总领事，
上海。

亲爱的Butrick先生：

我想报告昨晚对我发出的另一次威胁。威胁来自一名外国人，我有充分理由相信他是日本陆军特务部的雇员，名叫Nathaniel Rabin，据信是一名来自哈尔滨的俄籍犹太人，尽管他试图冒充美国人。

昨天，7月29日晚上10时30分，Rabin致电XNHA广播电台。值班播音员Frank Moss先生接听了电话。Rabin拒绝透露姓名，告诉播音员转告我，我只有三天时间停播。

Moss将此信息告知我，同时宣布他知道打电话的人是谁。他说那是他 personally 认识的Nathaniel Rabin。他陈述，他听出了他的声音，并敢发誓那就是Rabin。Moss告知我，他曾问Rabin为什么不亲自给我打电话传达信息。

今天凌晨约1时20分，我在家里睡觉时被电话吵醒。一个外国人的声音重复了给Moss的信息，即我只有三天时间停播。根据Moss先生给我的提示，我称呼来电者为Rabin。他问我怎么知道他的名字，我告诉他我听出了他的声音。然后他说：“我是谁有什么关系。你有三天时间停播。” 随后他摔下了听筒。

我已向警方报告了该威胁，我认为最好同时通知您。

鉴于Moss所作的陈述，即他

page_data.en:
-2-
recognized Rabin's voice and in view of the man's reply
when I challenged him, I am convinced that he is the man
who telephoned.
It also is known that he returned to Shanghai
from North China about two weeks ago. Although he seldom
appears south of Soochow Creek, he was seen by myself in the
lobby of the Foreign Y.M.C.A. last Sunday.
Sincerely,
Carroll D. Alsott.

North Szechuen Road, at 5 p.m., April 29, 1940.
    It has now been ascertained that the American
woman mentioned in Special Branch report dated
May 29, 1940, as being associated with Kraft alias
Durkop alias Durock, is not the wife of von Hanvel
but is the wife of Charles Melchers of Transocean
News Service, who was formerly an employee of the
Shanghai Waterworks Company. It is stated that
Mrs. Melchers is extremely anti-British and harbours
a grudge against the Waterworks Company in connection
with the termination of her husband's services with
that concern. This American woman is of German
extraction and her maiden name was also Kraft.
    Information was also received to the effect
that the local German Authorities, who have one
or more radio transmitting and receiving sets in
the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Schule, Avenue Haig, through
their Russian engineer, unsuccessfully attempted
to buy a raido antenna from the manager of Station
X.M.H.A. on the morning of May 30, 1940.

Reference Special Branch report on the
above subject dated May 26, 1940, in which
reference is made to two German Gestapo agents,
namely, Kraft and Durock, it has now been learned
that Kraft and Durock are one and the same person
and that he also uses the name Durkop or Durcop.
Kraft is reported to be utilizing an American
woman who is married to a German (it has not
been possible to ascertain this lady's name but
she may possibly be the wife of von Hanvel, Park
Hotel), in his activities but details are lacking.
Information has been received from the same
source to the effect that on the evening of
May 28, 1940, Kraft was making merry around the
town in celebration of a deal which he had just
arranged, for the transporting to Germany via the
Siberian railway, of 1,000 tons (?) of aluminium
packed in tea chests. According to this
information the aluminium is being packed in tea
chests somewhere in the Western district and
shipped in Japanese ships.

Information from the same source is to the
effect one Winkelmann (Dutch) husband of Ann
Summers and son of the Dutch General Winkelmann
is actively pro-Nazi and is associated with a
German named Ernst Grossmann, 153 Route des Soeurs.

Shanghai. 15.4.40

Dear Sir:
The interruptions on your radio are to be expected. For many months
I have been amazed, that you allowed Mr.Alcott to drag you into political
currents. His News talks are interesting, but obviously propaganda, which
means were he not getting money from the Chungking Government he would not
put over such bitter and one-sided Chinese propaganda . That "Jello" etc
are but cloaks to get his Chungkung stuff over.

The municipal election played right into his hand and he fought the
local election on the strength of the Chungking money.

We know that men come to China to get xxxx money as quickly as they
can and get out, but that you , an established, and hope-to-be-staple-
business should allow anyone to jeopardize your business un-necessarily
beats we people who advertise with you and who have helped you to build that
business.

We, no matter what our local war hopes may be, know that the Japanese
have control of China... the price of everything local tell us this... so why
in the name of common business sense allow Allcott to fill us up with
Chinese paid propaganda as to this and that (supposed) victory of the Chinese
army when we know it does not exist and when it led you into certain
unpopularity and your advertisers off the air.

You have been asking for it and you have got it. That it did not come
to you before beats me. Now ask yourself why you got it? and you have the
answer.... because you allowed a man to deaf, dumb and blind you.

Not content with this, he has the effrontry, and you the dumbness, to
turn this latest affair into a personal propaganda appeal. Who in heavens name
wants "listeners protests" but Alcott himself as his personal boost fan mail.

It has come to this that we are wondering who is X.M.H.A. and we say
The Chungking Government and their mouth-piece Allcott, who, all power to him
if he can get it over, is too slick even for himself because he will take
both himself and you off the air permanently, if not checked by you.
for your advertisers will not continue to fight political battles.

All along he has treated you as a mutt, now he is treating the public
likewise. And should this not dawn on you, I intend to take up this matter
in the daily press, for we want harmony , or as much of it as white men can
give.. in this settlement. He has just about pulled the last straw from his
sheaf and we some of us will help him bring you to a common sense basis if you
are ready to do so at once.

Wake up your country needs you.

上海。1940 年 4 月 15 日

尊敬的先生：
贵电台受到的干扰是意料之中的。几个月来，我一直感到惊讶，您竟然允许阿尔科特（Alcott）先生将您卷入政治潮流。他的新闻谈话很有趣，但显然是宣传，这意味着如果他没有从重庆政府拿钱，他就不会播出如此尖刻和片面的中国宣传。那些“吉露果冻（Jello）”等赞助不过是掩盖他传播重庆内容的幌子。

市政选举正好正中他的下怀，他依靠重庆的资金参与了地方选举的争斗。

我们知道有些人来中国是为了尽快赚取 xxxx 钱然后离开，但是像您这样一家 established（原文如此，意为既定的/老牌的），且希望成为支柱的企业，竟然允许任何人不必要地危及您的业务，这让我们要为您做广告并帮助您建立业务的广告商们感到难以理解。

无论我们对本地战争的期望如何，我们都知道日本人控制着中国……本地一切物品的价格都告诉了我们这一点……那么，看在常识性商业理智的份上，为什么还要允许阿尔科特用所谓中国军队的各种（所谓的）胜利来给我们灌输由中国付费的宣传呢？我们知道这些胜利并不存在，而且这导致您遭受了某些不受欢迎，并使您的广告商停止投放广告。

这是您自找的，您也得到了。在此之前没找上您才让我吃惊。现在问问自己为什么会这样？答案就有了……因为您允许一个人让您变得耳聋、眼瞎、无知。

他不满足于此，还厚颜无耻地，而您也麻木不仁地，将最近的事件变成个人的宣传诉求。天知道除了阿尔科特本人将其作为个人提升的粉丝邮件外，谁想要“听众抗议”。

事情已经发展到我们在怀疑 X.M.H.A. 到底是谁，我们说，是重庆政府及其喉舌阿尔科特，如果他能把这招使出来，那他确实厉害，但他甚至对自己来说也太圆滑了，因为如果不加制止，他将把您和他自己都永久地赶出电波。因为您的广告商不会继续参与政治斗争。

一直以来他都把您当傻瓜对待，现在他也这样对待公众。如果您还不醒悟，我打算在日报上提出此事，因为我们希望在这个租界里实现和谐，或者至少实现白人所能给予的那种和谐。他刚刚抽走了他束中的最后一根稻草，如果您愿意立即这样做，我们中的一些人将帮助您将局面恢复到常识基础之上。

醒来吧，您的国家需要您。

Reference Chengtu Road Misc. Report 207/40
on the above subject, D.S.I. Black and D.S.I. Logan
called on Mr. Healey, Manager of Radio Station X.M.H.A.
at 10 a.m. May 25, 1940, and interviewed him further
in regard to the threats which had been made against
his station. Mr. Healey stated that he was unable
to divulge the source of his information that local
Nazis would bomb his station but reiterated that it
came from a reliable source in one of the local
intelligence services. He produced a copy of a
letter dated May 15, 1940, which purported to come
from a Nazi source, which accused him of being a running
dog of the Allies and threatened dire punishment for
him in the not distant future, when local conditions
will be much changed. As the original letter had
been handed to Mr. Carol Alcott (News Commentator)
together with previous threatening letters which had
been received, it was not possible to obtain them
but Mr. Healey has promised to place them in the
hands of the Police as soon as he can get them back
from Mr. Alcott.

Mr. Healey also stated that he had received
information to the effect that two German Gestapo
agents, named Kraft and Durock, who formerly occupied
Room 309 of the Imperial Hotel, Tokyo, came to
Shanghai about March 24 and have since been living
in Room 508, Broadway Mansions. Ostensibly their

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
No. J. B. D. 6813/14/5 (7)
Date

American Radio Station
Here Protests Against
Japanese Interference

Alleging deliberate interference by Japanese elements in Hongkew with the wave-length of the American-owned radio Station XMHA, Mr. L. E. Healey, station manager, and Mr. Carroll D. Alcott, commentator whose independent news broadcast and commentary goes out over the air from the same station, yesterday lodged a protest with Mr. Richard T. Butrick, United States Acting Consul-General in Shanghai.

At the same time, the station manager and the commentator requested that the matter be placed before the Japanese authorities in an effort to have the interference stopped.

The interference was still on the air at a late hour last night, having started in the morning and continued throughout the day. On one occasion, Station XHMA changed its wave-length from 60 kilocycles to 65 kilocycles or broadcast. The interference followed suit and the jamming was renewed.

Jam Short-Wave Also

Late yesterday afternoon, interference with the short-wave frequency operated by XMHA also started and another complaint was lodged by Mr. Alcott with Mr. Butrick. The Japanese Consulate-General was informed by Mr. Butrick of the interference on long-wave yesterday afternoon and the Japanese are stated to have promised to investigate the matter. The investigation, however, brought no results yesterday.

As a result of the interference, hundreds of complaints poured into XMHA throughout the day. Listeners all over the city complained that not only were Mr. Alcott's broadcasts being jammed out by the interference but other programs were being interfered with as well.

In a statement to the press last night, Mr. Alcott declared:

"There is no question but what this a deliberate attempt to drive me from the air, at least during the present election campaign period in Shanghai. With the means at our disposal, we have traced the point from which the interference is coming to an area in Hongkew near Chapoo and North Soochow Roads.

"The interference was first noticed four days ago but at that time, it was comparatively mild and confined largely to the hours of my broadcasts," Mr. Alcott continued. "It is significant that the interference started at about the same time I came out in open support of the five British and two American status quo candidates standing for election to the Shanghai Municipal Council as opposed to the five Japanese candidates.

"That those responsible for the interference have no legal grounds for complaint is clearly evidenced by the methods they have used in their efforts to drive me and the station from the air," Mr. Alcott said. "If they had legal grounds, there are legal means of taking action against me or the station."

"The Japanese have repeatedly claimed that they do not intend to establish a dictatorial system in the administration of International Settlement affairs should they obtain five seats on the Shanghai Municipal Council," said Mr. Alcott. "Granting that this might be true, the deliberate suppression of news and opinion by interference with radio broadcasts can hardly be regarded as lending much support to this claim," the commentator concluded.

The interference was also hindering the sending of messages to and reception from Manila. It was reported last night by cable companies here. It is understood that they are also making a protest about the matter.

编号 J. B. D. 6813/14/5 (7)
日期

美国广播电台
在此抗议日本干涉

美国_owned_广播电台 XMHA 经理 L. E. Healey 先生，以及在该台播出独立新闻广播和评论的评论员 Carroll D. Alcott 先生，指控虹口地区的日本势力故意干扰该台波长，昨日向美国驻上海代理总领事 Richard T. Butrick 先生提出抗议。

与此同时，电台经理和评论员请求将此事项提交日本当局，以努力停止干扰。

直到昨晚深夜，干扰仍在空中持续，该干扰始于早晨并持续了一整天。有一次，XHMA 电台将其波长从60千周改为65千周进行广播。干扰随之改变，干扰再次恢复。

短波也受干扰

昨天下午晚些时候，XMHA 运营的短波频率也开始受到干扰，Alcott 先生向 Butrick 先生提出了另一项投诉。Butrick 先生已于昨天下午将长波受干扰情况告知日本总领事馆，据悉日本人承诺调查此事。然而，昨天的调查没有结果。

由于干扰，全天有数百起投诉涌入 XMHA。全市各地的听众抱怨说，不仅 Alcott 先生的广播被干扰切断，其他节目也受到干扰。

Alcott 先生昨晚在向媒体发表的声明中宣称：

“毫无疑问，这是一次蓄意企图将我赶出电波，至少是在上海目前的竞选活动期间。利用我们现有的手段，我们将干扰源追踪到了虹口靠近乍浦路和北苏州路的一个区域。

“四天前首次注意到干扰，但当时干扰相对轻微，主要局限于我的广播时段，” Alcott 先生继续说道。“值得注意的是，干扰开始的时间大致与我公开支持竞选上海工部局董事的五名维持现状派英国候选人和两名美国候选人、反对五名日本候选人的时间相同。

“那些负责干扰的人没有任何法律依据进行投诉，这从他们试图将我和电台赶出电波所使用的方法中可以清楚地看出，” Alcott 先生说。“如果他们有法律依据，就有法律手段对我或电台采取行动。”

“日本人一再声称，如果他们获得上海工部局董事会的五个席位，并不打算在国际租界事务管理中建立独裁制度，” Alcott 先生说。“即便这可能是真的，通过干扰无线电广播来故意压制新闻和舆论，很难被视为对这一主张有多大支持，”这位评论员总结道。

干扰也阻碍了向马尼拉发送信息和从马尼拉接收信息。据本地电报公司昨晚报道。据悉，他们也就此事提出抗议。
