Interference
With XMHA
Is Continued

Interference with the wave-length
of the American-owned radio station
XMHA continued yesterday, with
renewed efforts to blot out broad-
casts to Shanghailanders.
Little result, however, was gained
by these attempts to stifle programs
allegedly considered "provocative"
by some quarters. It was expected
that the interference would continue
today, but would soon be stopped.
Mr. L. H. Healey, station manager,
and Mr. Carroll D. Alcott, com-
mentator, on Saturday lodged a
formal protest with the American
Acting Consul-General here, Mr.
Richard T. Butrick. The protest
alleged that Japanese elements
operating from Hongkew were in-
stigating the interference.
It was also requested that the
matter be laid before the Japanese
authorities, in an effort to have the
interference halted. The Japanese
are expected to issue an answer
today.

Successful Dodge

The station officials revealed yes-
terday that the interference was be-
ing comparatively successfully
dodged. Since XMHA's radio beam
is interfered with at about the time
that Mr. Alcott's news broadcast
and commentary goes on the air,
station engineers have effected the
technique of slightly shifting the
wave-length suddenly a few minutes
before the broadcast.
Shanghailanders reported yester-
day that they were receiving the
broadcasts well, and had "caught
on" to the dodge. Since it takes
the rival radio beam almost half an
hour to catch up with the new
wave-length, little is achieved by
the interference.

Began Saturday

The interference began Saturday
morning and lasted all through
that day, while the short-wave
frequency operated in a big way by
XMHA was also the object of inter-
ference.
The campaign of intervention
began significantly "at about the
same time I came out in open sup-
port of the five British and two
American status quo candidates
standing for election to the Shang-
hai Municipal Council as opposed
to the five Japanese candidates,"
Mr. Alcott declared in a statement,
charging that "this is a deliberate
attempt to drive me from the air,
at least during the present election
campaign period."
Point from which the interference
was coming was traced to an area
in Hongkew near Chapoo and North
Soochow Roads, Mr. Alcott said.
Hongkew, too, is the area most
severely affected by the interference,
it was said.

1946年
上海公共租界工部局警务处
编号：S. B. D. 6813/14/X/17
日期

对XMHA电台的干扰
仍在继续

针对美资广播电台XMHA波长的干扰昨日仍在继续，各方再次试图阻断向上海外侨（Shanghailanders）播出的节目。然而，这些旨在压制被某些方面指称为“挑衅性”节目的企图收效甚微。预计今日干扰仍将持续，但不久后将停止。电台经理L. H. Healey先生和评论员Carroll D. Alcott先生于上周六向驻沪美国代理总领事Richard T. Butrick先生提出正式抗议。抗议称，位于虹口（Hongkew）的日本势力正在煽动此次干扰。

此外，还请求将此事项提交日本当局，以期停止干扰。预计日方将于今日作出答复。

成功规避

电台官员昨日透露，干扰已被相对成功地规避。由于XMHA电台的无线电波束在Alcott先生的新闻广播和评论开播时受到干扰，电台工程师采取了一种技术手段，即在广播开始前几分钟突然微调波长。

上海外侨昨日报告称，他们能清晰地接收广播，并已“识破”了这一规避手法。由于敌对无线电波束需要近半小时才能追踪到新的波长，因此干扰行动成效寥寥。

始于周六

干扰始于周六上午，并持续了一整天，同时XMHA大力运营的短波频率也成为干扰对象。

Alcott先生在一份声明中称，这场干预行动的开始时间颇具深意，“大约就在我公开支持竞选上海工部局董事会的五名英国候选人和两名美国现状派候选人、以反对五名日本候选人的时候”，他指控称“这是故意试图将我赶出电波，至少是在目前的选举竞选期间”。

Alcott先生表示，干扰源已被追踪至虹口（Hongkew）靠近乍浦路（Chapoo Road）和北苏州路（North Soochow Road）的区域。据说，虹口也是受干扰影响最严重的地区。

Sir,
At 10 p.m. 18/1/40 Mr. C. Alcott, News Commentator for Station XMHA telephoned the station from No. 445 Race Course Road reporting, that whilst travelling in his private ricsna on Race Course Road near Taku Road he had been stopped by two male Japanese.

On receipt of this message, the undersigned proceeded to No. 445 Race Course Road and interviewed the complainant, when the following was ascertained.

At about 9.45 p.m. even date Mr. Alcott left the Shanghai Times Building situated at 160 Ave. Rd. VII (where he resides) in his private ricsna, in order to proceed to Station XMHA at 445 Race Course Road for the night's news commentary, he travelled along Ave. Rd. VII, Yu Ya Ching Road turning into Race Course Road as is his usual procedure. On arrival at the intersection of Race Course Road and Taku Road, a large grey sedan car, suddenly drove out from Taku Road stopping immediately in front of Mr. Alcott's ricsha, causing the ricsha coolie to stop suddenly.

As the car made no inclination to move, Mr. Alcott, ordered his ricsha coolie to pass around the front of the car. The driver of the car, noticing the ricsha coolie's actions, drove his car a little bit further and again stopped, thereby blocking the ricsha from proceeding West.

At this point Mr. Alcott noticed that the occupants of the car were two male Japanese, dressed in Japanese Military Uniform, who were closely scrutinizing him.

1940年1月18日晚上10时，XMHA电台新闻评论员C. Alcott先生从跑马厅路445号致电巡捕房报告称，当他乘坐私人人力车（ricsna）在跑马厅路靠近大沽路（Taku Road）路段行驶时，被两名日本男子拦下。

接到此消息后，卑职前往跑马厅路445号会见投诉人，查明情况如下。

同日晚上约9时45分，Alcott先生乘坐私人人力车（ricsna）离开位于爱多亚路160号的《字林西报》大楼（其居住地），前往跑马厅路445号的XMHA电台进行夜间新闻评论。他沿爱多亚路、虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）行驶，按惯例转入跑马厅路。当到达跑马厅路与大沽路交叉口时，一辆大型灰色轿车突然从大沽路驶出，立即停在Alcott先生的人力车前，导致人力车夫紧急停车。

由于该车没有移动的迹象，Alcott先生命令人力车夫从车前绕过去。轿车司机注意到人力车夫的举动，将车向前开了一点，再次停下，从而阻挡人力车向西行进。

此时，Alcott先生注意到车内有两名身穿日本军服的日本男子，他们正在仔细打量他。

1941年3月25日上午6时35分，在跑马厅路445号X.M.H.A.广播电台前门外执勤的中国巡捕（C.P.C.）暂时离开（将另一起案件带往警局）期间，中国巡捕第2165号目睹两名华籍男子正在撬动该处所前门上的挂锁。他喝令这两名男子，二人随即逃窜。该中国巡捕展开追捕，当逃跑者仍无视其停下的喝令时，他开枪射击两发，其中一发击中并致伤其中一名男子，该男子随后被捕。（参见成都路首次报告 353/41）。

除了上述事件发生在跑马厅路445号广播电台外这一事实外，没有理由相信这两名华籍男子除盗窃广播电台前门外的黄铜挂锁外还有其他意图。（被捕男子被发现持有3把黄铜挂锁，疑似从其他地址窃得）。

在就上述案件进行现场调查时，获悉中国巡捕第2200号于1941年3月25日上午8时30分左右，在该广播电台加高的水泥台阶与外侧前门之间的缝隙中，捡到了一发未击发的.45口径自动手枪子弹。鉴于上述事件中使用的唯一手枪为.380口径柯尔特手枪（中国警佐第2168号的配枪），这发子弹的来源便成了问题。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处）

radio station at about 8.30 a.m. 25/3/41. As the only

X.N.N.A.广播电台经理 F.L. Healey 先生断言，他确信前一晚子弹并不在（被发现的那个）位置，因为他在1941年3月24日离开电台前曾检查过加高的台阶（防洪措施）。Carrol Alcott 先生也接受了具名人的问询，因为已知他有时携带.45口径柯尔特手枪。Alcott 先生坚决否认丢失过子弹或该子弹属于他。
    这发子弹已被送往武器鉴定科进行检查，相关报告将在适当时候收到。然而，武器鉴定科科长、副督察 Ewins O. 口头告知具名人，该子弹是1936年美国弗兰克福德兵工厂（Frankford Arsenal）制造的.45口径柯尔特自动手枪子弹，据信与已知由 Alcott 先生持有的同批子弹相同。
    推测这发涉事子弹可能是 Alcott 先生在之前某个时间（在他不知情的情况下）掉落的，并且可能在两名窃贼强行撬动门锁时，因门的震动而从其所在的灰尘中被震出。

6/Sheet No. 3.

the dust in which it lay by the jarring of the door,
whilst the two thieves were forcing the padlock on
the door. This, admittedly, is pure conjecture, but
appears to be the only logical explanation.

Whilst interviewing Mr. E.L. Healey at the
radio station, latter informed the undersigned of an
anonymous telephone message of threatening nature
he had received the previous evening (24/3/41).

At 5.30 p.m. 24/3/41, Mr. Healey states he
answered the telephone at the radio station, when a
male foreigner, speaking good English (like an
American's voice) asked to speak with the manager of
the station. Mr. Healey replied that he was the
station manager. The caller then said, "I want to
tell you that we are going to shoot you and also Mr.
Alcott". Mr. Healey says he replied, "Go ahead,
we'll be waiting for you". The caller then hung up
his receiver.

At 10.30 a.m. 25/3/41 Mr. C. Alcott telephoned
the Officer i/c stating that he had just received
information (he did not state the source) that certain
persons had made plans to bomb both Radio Station XHA
and the office of the Ta Mei Wan Pao (大美晚報) 255
Weihaiwei Road on the 25/3/41.

在广播电台采访 E.L. Healey 先生时，后者告知具名人，他在前一天晚上（1941年3月24日）收到了一条匿名的威胁性电话留言。

Healey 先生称，1941年3月24日下午5时30分，他在广播电台接听电话，一名外语流利（声音像美国人）的外籍男子要求与电台经理通话。Healey 先生回答说他就是电台经理。来电者随后说：“我想告诉你，我们要枪杀你，还有 Alcott 先生。” Healey 先生说他回答说：“来吧，我们等着你们。” 来电者随后挂断了电话。

1941年3月25日上午10时30分，C. Alcott 先生致电负责警官，称他刚刚收到消息（未说明来源），某些人计划于1941年3月25日轰炸 XHA 广播电台和位于威海卫路255号的《大美晚报》办公室。

At 11.40 a.m. on March 24, 1941, Mr. C. Alcott
of Radio Station X.W.H.A., 445 Race Course Road, re-
ported to Chengtu Road Station, by telephone, that he
had been the recipient of a further anonymous letter
which was of a threatening nature.
On being interviewed by the undersigned Mr.
Alcott stated that the letter was addressed to him
at the Radio Station and came through the post at
9.45 a.m. even date. It reads:-
Mr. Alcott:
    We beg to inform you that at a meeting
of the Italian Fascist party in Shanghai
about one week ago you were condemned and
attempts will be made on your life on the
pretence that insults to fascism are broad-
casted by you. To protect yourself, you
may inform your hearers of all this.
                            Italia Libera
March 20th, 1941.
The envelope bears four one-cent stamps, and
was posted at the General Post Office, North Sze-
chuen Road, on March 23, 1941.

its source, but there is no signature or clue to the

At 10 a.m. 21-3-41, the undersigned interviewed
Mr. C. Alcott at Radio Station X.M.H.A., 445 Race
Course Road, with a view to being present during an
interview between Mr. Alcott and a foreign female as
referred to in diary 3. However, from Mr. Alcott it
was learned that at about 8.30 p.m. 20-3-41, the female
in question paid a surprise visit to the station and
the interview took place. This station was not
informed.

The female identified herself as Mrs. Squibb,
Russian, wife of Mr. Squibb, an employee of the
British Embassy Office (The Shanghai Directory gives
Mr. A. T. Squibb as a naval liaison officer attached
to the British Embassy Offices, 27 The Bund, and,
according to the Shanghai Telephone Directory, resides
at 37 Broadway Mansions, telephone No. 40731). She
emphasized the fact that her husband was not aware
of the interview.

Refusing to divulge the source of her information
Mrs. Squibb proceeded to warn Mr. Alcott to take every
precaution by means of changing his routes of travel
daily; that certain Italians would make a definite
attempt on his life in the near future; that his M/Car
was being followed nightly and immediately a favourable

1941年3月21日上午10时，具名人在跑马厅路445号 X.M.H.A. 广播电台采访了 C. Alcott 先生，旨在旁听 Alcott 先生与一名外籍女性的会面，如日志3所述。然而，从 Alcott 先生处得知，该名女性于1941年3月20日晚上8时30分左右突然造访电台，会面已经发生。电台方面未获通知。

该女性自称 Squibb 夫人，俄罗斯人，是英国大使馆办事处雇员 Squibb 先生的妻子（《上海名录》显示 A. T. Squibb 先生为附属于外滩27号英国大使馆办事处的海军联络官，且根据《上海电话簿》，其居住于百老汇大厦37号，电话号码40731）。她强调其丈夫并不知道这次会面。

Squibb 夫人拒绝透露信息来源，进而警告 Alcott 先生要通过每天改变出行路线来采取一切预防措施；某些意大利人将在不久的将来对他的生命进行明确的尝试；他的摩托车每晚都被跟踪，一旦有利

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处）
（批注：hughs）

opportunity offered, he would be shot.
Mrs. Squibb appeared to be well informed, she being
able to outline recent routes taken and places visited
by Mr. Alcott.
Although she refused to give the source of
information, on leaving, promised to give names of
persons concerned in the near future.
On arriving home later, Mr. Alcott learned from
his wife that she had received a telephone call from
Mrs. Squibb who asked that she not inform Mr. Alcott
of the call but to request him to take every precaution
in the near future, and also suggested that Mr. Alcott
visit a Mr. Boekevinder, a fortune-teller, who would
give all necessary information (The Shanghai Telephone
Directory gives S. Boekebinder, 941 Bubbling Well Road,
telephone No. 39904).
Mr. Alcott states his W/Car was not followed p.m.
20-3-41 and he will not take any further precautions
other than continued change of route.
With reference to the W/Car License No. 11039 which
followed Mr. Alcott's W/Car on the night of 17-3-41 (see
diary 2), it is now ascertained that the number is
11059, a maroon sedan, Mr. Alcott having again seen the
W/Car at 5.45 p.m. 20-3-41, proceeding West along Avenue
Edward VII near the Nanking Theatre.

机会出现，他就会被枪杀。
Squibb 夫人似乎消息灵通，她能勾勒出 Alcott 先生最近走过的路线和去过的地方。
虽然她拒绝提供信息来源，但在离开时承诺在不久的将来提供相关人员的姓名。
Alcott 先生稍后回到家时，从妻子处得知她接到了 Squibb 夫人的电话，Squibb 夫人要求她不要告诉 Alcott 先生有过这通电话，而是请求他在不久的将来采取一切预防措施，并建议 Alcott 先生拜访一位名叫 Boekevinder 的算命先生，此人将提供所有必要信息（《上海电话簿》显示 S. Boekebinder，地址为静安寺路941号，电话号码39904）。
Alcott 先生表示，他的汽车在1941年3月20日下午并未被跟踪，除了继续改变路线外，他不会采取其他进一步的预防措施。

At 2 p.m. 20/3/41, Mr. C. Alcott, News Commentator

came to the station and handed the Officer i/c, a

"Dear Sir,
        I know you are a stamp collectiouer. May
I offer you this new specimen from the southern
part of the Axis. I schall not forget to send
you the northen one as soon as I'll get it. As
for the Axis itself, you may be sure you schall
feel it striking on your damned bloody head in a
very very near future!
Believe me, please, very sincerely and truly yours

he had received the letter at about 9 a.m. 20/3/41 at

the envelope has been mislaid and was probably

先生，
    关于此档案，X.M.H.A.广播电台评论员C. 奥尔科特（C. Alcott）先生于今天——1941年3月18日——上午10:30向卑职报告称，3月17日晚，他被一辆私家车跟踪，该车由一名外国人驾驶，车内载有四名外国乘客。
    奥尔科特先生称，他于3月17日晚上约10:50离开X.M.H.A.广播电台；与其中籍保镖一同上车，并指示其中籍司机送他回家。车辆沿威海卫路向西行驶，当接近成都路时，奥尔科特先生称他注意到一辆深褐色轿车停在威海卫路南侧，驶出到路中间并开始跟随他的车。据奥尔科特先生称，车内有五名外国人，其中一人驾驶。就他所能辨认的而言，车牌号码是11039。
    奥尔科特先生接着补充说，到达西摩路（Seymour Road）时，他指示司机向南转入西摩路，为了确定那辆车是否真的在跟踪他们，又转入了法租界的几条小马路。正如他所怀疑的那样，

however, no matter what turning they took, so did the
car containing the foreigners.

Finally, on reaching Rue Paul Henry in the vicinity
of his home Mr. Alcott instructed his chauffeur to
swing his car across the roadway, thinking that if the
occupants of the pursuing car were genuine they would
stop. However, as the chauffeur did this the car
contained the foreigners mounted the pavement - the
only way they could pass without stopping - and
disappeared.

As a precautionary measure when stopping his car,
Mr. Alcott states that he and his bodyguard drew their
pistols.

A check on W/Car Lic. No. 11039 through the
Traffic Office revealed that the car licenced under
that number was a Baby Austin owned by a Chinese. In
view of this it is presumed that Mr. Alcott did not
note the number of this dark brown sedan correctly.

Forwarded for information.

然而，无论他们如何转弯，那辆载有外国人的车也都跟着转弯。

最后，当到达靠近他家的保罗·亨利路（Rue Paul Henry）时，奥尔科特先生指示司机将车横在路面上，心想如果追赶者是无辜的，他们就会停下来。然而，当司机这样做时，那辆载有外国人的车开上了人行道——这是他们不停车就能通过的唯一方式——然后消失了。

奥尔科特先生称，作为停车时的预防措施，他和他的保镖拔出了手枪。

通过交通股对私家车牌照号码11039进行的核查显示，该号码注册的是一辆由一名中国人拥有的Baby Austin牌汽车。鉴于此，推测奥尔科特先生没有正确记下这辆深褐色轿车的号码。

Sergeant Sevenoaks submitted a report (copy
attached) giving the foregoing details, and the

was detailed to investigate further, with the result
that the following was ascertained:

The m/car in question, C.M.P. Lic. No. 11149, is
a black four seater Chevrolet roadster, and according
to Traffic Office records is owned by an Italian
named Mr. P. CORIGLIANO, residing at 312 Rue du Roi
Albert, French Concession.

saw the car at 10.20 p.m. A foreigner was driving,

（印章：特别处）

先生，

1941年3月16日晚上11:15下班时，华捕1664号向成都路站值班警长塞文奥克斯（Sevenoaks）报告称，同日晚上10:30，他在跑马厅路445号X.M.H.A.广播电台外执勤时，观察到一辆牌照号码为11149的汽车，由一名外国人驾驶，在附近行为非常可疑。

塞文奥克斯警长提交了一份报告（副本附后），提供了上述细节以及车主的姓名和地址。

此后，副巡官桑布鲁克（Sambrook）受命进行进一步调查，结果查明如下：

涉案汽车，工部局牌照号码11149，是一辆黑色的四座雪佛兰敞篷跑车，根据交通股记录，车主为一名意大利人，名为P. CORIGLIANO先生，居住在法租界阿尔贝王路（Rue du Roi Albert）312号。

看来，上述巡捕首先在晚上10:20看到该车。一名外国人正在驾驶，

whilst another foreigner sat besides him as a
passenger. It passed the Radio Station from west
and proceeded as far as Chungking Road corner.
It then turned around and proceeded back west
in the direction of Mohawk Road. Here it again
turned around and proceeded past the Radio
Station to Chungking Road where it stopped for
about five minutes. In all, according to the
constable, the car passed him six times.

Finally, the foreigners parked the car near
Mohawk Road; alighted and walked along the north
side of Race Course Road, past the Radio Station,
in the direction of Chungking Road; returning a
few minutes later on the south side. As they
passed him the constable noticed that one was
wearing a grey woollen overcoat and the other a
grey foreign style suit.

On reaching Mohawk Road the foreigners boarded
their car, just as a man, whom the constable describes
as being of stout build (believed to be Mr. C. Alcott),
came out of the Radio Station and boarded his car.
As the latter drove away in an easterly direction, the
constable states that he observed the two foreigners
in m/car, l.i.c. No. 11149, follow him.

另一名外国人坐在他旁边作为乘客。该车从西边经过广播电台，一直开到重庆路路口。然后它掉头向西朝莫霍克路（Mohawk Road）方向返回。在这里它再次掉头，经过广播电台开往重庆路，在那里停了大约五分钟。总之，据该巡捕称，这辆车从他面前经过了六次。

最后，这些外国人将车停在莫霍克路附近；下车后沿着跑马厅路北侧，经过广播电台，朝重庆路方向走去；几分钟后从南侧返回。当他们经过时，巡捕注意到一人穿着灰色羊毛大衣，另一人穿着灰色西式西装。

到达莫霍克路时，这些外国人上了车，就在这时，一名被巡捕描述为体格粗壮的人（被认为是C. 奥尔科特先生）从广播电台出来并上了他的车。后者向东驶离时，该巡捕称他观察到那两名外国人乘坐牌照号码为11149的汽车跟随他。

Between 7 p.m. and 11 p.m. on March 16, 1941 I was
on duty outside the front entrance of the X.M.H.A. Radio
Station, 445 Race Course Road.
At about 10.20 p.m., same date, I observed a small
black sedan m/car, Lic. No. 11149, containing two foreigners,
proceeding east to west along Race Course Road. At Chungking
Road corner it turned around and proceeded back east to
Mohawk Road. Here it again turned around and proceeded passed
the radio station back to Chungking Road corner where it
stopped for about five minutes. It then turned back to
Mohawk Road, and in all made six trips passed the radio
station. Finally, it stopped at Mohawk Road and the two
foreign occupants, one dressed in grey woollen overcoat,
and the other in a grey foreign style suit, alighted and
walked along the North side of Race Course Road, passed the
radio station, to Chungking Road. They returned on the south
side and re-entered their car just as a heavy built foreigner
came out of the X.M.H.A. Radio Station and entered his car.
I observed the latter drive away in an easterly direction
followed by the two foreigners in m/car Lic. No. 11149.

Sd.    C.P.C. 1664.

This case came up for hearing before the S.S.D.
Court (Judge Liu) on the a.m. 26-3-41 when, after the
evidence had been heard, the case was remanded until
the a.m. 10-4-41 for trial.

With reference to the remarks of the D. O. "A"
on Diary I. The accused was conveyed to the Paulun
Hospital as, investigating detectives believed he was
mortally wounded and the only chance of saving his
life depended on immediate medical attention. For
this reason, D.O. Marsden gave instructions that
accused be taken to the Paulun Hospital rather than
the Police Hospital, where the journey might have
resulted in an immediate fatality.

The accused was briefly questioned in the Paulun
Hospital on the p.m. 26-3-41 and admitted that he
together with another pedhand-hawker were attempting
to steal the brass lock from 445 Race Course Road when
they were interrupted by the arrival of the P/Ce C.P.O.
He also admitted that the other three pad-locks, found
in his possession were stolen, but was unable to recall
(due to his weakened condition) from what places.
Questioned as to the name and address of his accomplice
he mumbled something unintelligible, but nodded when
the named Tsang ("f") was suggested to him. He said
his wife knew the man.

本案于1941年3月26日上午在特别市政法庭（刘法官）开庭审理，在听取证据后，案件被延期至1941年4月10日上午审判。

关于"A"区主管在日记I中的备注。被告被送往宝隆医院（Paulun Hospital），因为调查探员认为他受了致命伤，挽救他生命的唯一机会取决于立即获得医疗救治。出于这个原因，马尔斯登（Marsden）主管指示将被告送往宝隆医院而不是警察医院，因为前往警察医院的旅程可能会导致立即死亡。

1941年3月26日下午，被告在宝隆医院接受了简短讯问，并承认他与另一名小贩试图窃取跑马厅路445号的铜锁时，被中央巡捕房警官的到来打断。他还承认，在他身上发现的另外三把挂锁是偷来的，但由于身体虚弱，无法回忆是从什么地方偷来的。当被问及同伙的姓名和地址时，他含糊不清地嘟囔了一些话，但当向他提出曾（Tsang）("f")这个名字时，他点了点头。他说他的妻子认识这个人。

inquiries by D.J.I. Taylor and others 192
At 6.47 a.m. 25-3-41, P./C. C.P.C. 2165
telephoned to the station (Street Tel. Box 3. Mohawk
Road, Avenue Edward VII) reporting that he had just
shot one of two male Chinese, whom he had observed
attempting to break into Radio Station X.M.H.A. 445
Race Course Road and who had decamped when he
challenged them.
The ..... emergency ambulance was immediately
despatched to the scene. D.S. 147 Marsden, P.S. 364
Valley and ...... life attended and made initial
enquiries which revealed the following details.
At 6.35 a.m. 25-3-41, P./C. C.P.C. 2165 was
patrolling east along the North side of Race Course
Road, when he observed two male Chinese on the South
side of the road at the entrance of Radio Station
X.M.H.A., 445 Race Course Road. The men were
apparently trying to break into the premises as one
of them was armed with an iron bar with which they
were forcing the pad-lock on the front door.
It should here be explained, that, the premises
of Radio Station X.M.H.A. at 445 Race Course Road are
under special police protection in connection with
the numerous threats received by the foreign personnel
of this radio station. It was merely a coincidence
that the C.P.C. on duty at the front entrance of the
premises was absent from his post (taking another case
to the station) at the time the two thieves selected
to break into the premises.
However, the plain clothes C.P.C. (2165) was

D.J.I. Taylor 等人进行的查询 192
1941年3月25日上午6时47分，华捕巡长（P./C. C.P.C.）2165号
通过电话向警局报案（电话亭位于莫霍克路，爱德华七世大道，3号街电箱），报告称他刚刚枪击了两名中国男子中的一人，他此前发现这两人正试图闯入位于跑马厅路445号的X.M.H.A.广播电台，并在其喝止时逃窜。
……急救救护车立即被派往现场。警探副督察（D.S.）147号 Marsden、警佐（P.S.）364号 Valley 以及……生命救护员到场并进行了初步调查，查得以下细节。
1941年3月25日上午6时35分，华捕巡长（P./C. C.P.C.）2165号正沿跑马厅路北侧向东巡逻，此时他观察到两名中国男子在跑马厅路445号X.M.H.A.广播电台入口处的道路南侧。这两人显然正试图闯入该处所，因为其中一人手持一根铁棒，他们正用其撬动前门上的挂锁。
此处需说明的是，鉴于该广播电台外籍人员收到大量威胁，位于跑马厅路445号的X.M.H.A.广播电台处所受特别警务保护。恰逢两名窃贼选择此时闯入时，负责该处所前门执勤的制服华捕巡长不在岗位上（正将另一起案件的相关人员送往警局），这纯属巧合。
然而，便衣华捕巡长（2165号）

page_data.en:
L/2

unaware of the reason for the uniform P.C.s absence
from his post and, seeing the two men attempting to
break into the premises immediately drew his pistol and

the latter departed in a westerly direction along
Race Course Road and the P./C. S.P.C. crossed the road
in pursuit. He called on the men, several times to halt
also warning them that he would open fire if they failed
to stop however they continued to run. As they were
near the corner of Mohawk Road, L.P.C. 2165 fired one
shot at the running men, as this had no effect, he fired
another shot wounding one of the men.

He continued to run, turning South into Mohawk
Road where he was intercepted by C.D.C. 84
(Vangtsepee) who happened to be proceeding North on
Mohawk Road and saw the two men running. P./C. S.P.C.
2165 then left the injured man in custody of C.D.C. 84
whilst he went to Mohawk Road, Avenue Edward VII
intersection to telephone to the station.

Meanwhile C.P.C.s 1208 and 2939, who had been on
duty at the rear entrance of 445 Race Course Road
(located inside Lane 429 Race Course Road) had arrived
on the scene but the other man had already made good
his escape into the French Concession. The arrested
man was found in possession of 3 brass pad-locks
page_data.zh:
L/2

并不知晓制服巡长离岗的原因，看到两人试图闯入处所，他立即拔出手枪，

后者沿跑马厅路向西方向逃离，该华捕巡长（S.P.C.）穿过马路进行追捕。他多次喝令两人站住，并警告若不停止将开枪射击，但两人继续奔跑。当他们接近莫霍克路拐角时，华捕巡长（L.P.C.）2165号向奔跑中的男子开了一枪，因未见效，他又开了一枪，击中并致伤其中一人。

伤者继续奔跑，向南转入莫霍克路，在那里被华捕侦探（C.D.C.）84号（Vangtsepee，音译）拦截，该侦探当时正沿莫霍克路向北行进，目睹两人奔跑。随后，华捕巡长（S.P.C.）2165号将伤者交由华捕侦探84号看管，自己前往莫霍克路与爱德华七世大道交叉口处的电话亭向警局打电话。

与此同时，原本在跑马厅路445号后门（位于跑马厅路429弄内）执勤的华捕巡长1208号和2939号已抵达现场，但另一名男子已成功逃入法租界。被捕男子身上搜出3个黄铜挂锁，

page_data.en:
1/4.

apparently stolen from some other addresses.

Prior to his removal in the ambulance, detectives questioned the wounded man but, owing to his semi-conscious condition, could only learn his name which he stated was Tsai ( ) and address: 856 Rue Amiral Bayle, F.C.

He was placed in the ambulance and, escorted by F.S. Malley and C.P.C. 2108, removed to the Paulun Hospital where he was admitted and detained. The following medical certificate was issued :-

"Bullet wounds. The bullet entered in the region of the buttocks and penetrated through the abdomen, forcing out and expelling the bowels."

The undersigned and C.D.S. 192 continued enquiries and, with the assistance of the French Police, proceeded to 856 Rue Amiral Bayle which was found to be a small tailor shop. None of the inmates knew of anyone with the name of Tsai, who resided in the house. However, one of the tailors, Wei Kung Yoong ( ) consented to accompany detectives to try and identify the person.

On visiting the Paulun Hospital, the tailor recognised the patient as a 2nd hand-hawker (name unknown) who, with his wife, occupied a 1st floor left room at 856 Rue A. Bayle. Subsequently, detectives located the injured man's wife, Tsai Yee Sz ( )
page_data.zh:
1/4.

显然是从其他地址偷来的。

在被救护车送走之前，侦探讯问了受伤男子，但由于其处于半昏迷状态，仅得知其自称姓蔡（Tsai，音译），住址为：法租界贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）856号。

他被送上救护车，由法医警佐（F.S.）Malley 和华捕巡长2108号护送，送往宝隆医院（Paulun Hospital），该院予以收治并拘留。出具了以下医疗证明：

“枪弹伤。子弹从臀部区域射入，穿透腹部，导致肠管脱出。”

签署人及华捕侦探警佐（C.D.S.）192号继续调查，并在法国警察的协助下，前往贝勒路856号，发现那是一家小裁缝店。店内无人认识居住在该处的姓蔡之人。然而，其中一名裁缝魏公永（Wei Kung Yoong，音译）同意陪同侦探前去辨认此人。

在探访宝隆医院时，该裁缝认出病人是一名二手货小贩（姓名不详），他与妻子居住在贝勒路856号二楼左间。随后，侦探找到了伤者的妻子蔡氏（Tsai Yee Sz，音译），

page_data.en:
1/5.

who was also taken to the Paulun Hospital and there
identified the patient as her husband:- Tsai Sien Zang
(      ) 37, Anhwei, M/2nd hand-hawker, 856 Rue A.
Bayle.

Further questioning of the female obtained the
information that her husband had left home at about
5.30 a.m. (25/3/41) in company with another 2nd hand-
hawker named Tsang (    ). She further stated that her
husband and Tsang always worked together and, that for
the past 3 or 4 mornings, they had gone out in the early
morning. She could furnish no information as to Tsang's
address but stated he could usually be located at the
end of Rue Bluntschli or in company with other 2nd
hand-hawkers on this thoroughfare.

Detectives accompanied the female on a tour of
places frequented by 2nd hand-hawkers on Rue Bluntschli
F.C. in an effort to arrest Tsang but without success,
this man apparently having avoided his usual haunts.

A further visit to the Paulun Hospital found the
injured man still in a semi-conscious state and the
attending physician said his condition was critical
and likely to prove fatal. The patient's finger-prints
were secured and the Dr. handed over the bullet which
had penetrated through the man's abdomen and was found
page_data.zh:
1/5.

她也被带到宝隆医院，并在那里指认病人为其丈夫：蔡先章（Tsai Sien Zang，音译），37岁，安徽人，职业为二手货小贩，住址贝勒路856号。

通过对该女子的进一步讯问，获知其丈夫于1941年3月25日凌晨5时30分左右，与另一名名为曾（Tsang，音译）的二手货小贩一同离家。她还陈述，其丈夫与曾某总是共同工作，且在过去的三四个早晨，他们都在清晨外出。她无法提供曾某的住址，但称通常可在布伦茨利路（Rue Bluntschli）尽头或在该大路上与其他二手货小贩在一起时找到他。

侦探陪同该女子巡视了法租界布伦茨利路上二手货小贩常去的地方，试图逮捕曾某，但未成功，此人似乎避开了其常去之处。

再次探访宝隆医院时，发现受伤男子仍处于半昏迷状态，主治医生表示其病情危重，可能致命。提取了患者的指纹，医生交出了穿透该男子腹部并在其衣物中发现的子弹，

page_data.en:
1/6.

in his clothes.
    D.P.S. 83 Cockburn took the two cartridge cases
(found at the scene) and the spent bullet to the Arms
Identification Section, together with C.P.C. 2165's
service pistol (S.M.P. No. 1638) for examination. A
report on the result will be received in due course.
    The accused's finger-prints were also forwarded
to the Finger Print Bureau where it was found they
had the following previous record :-
Attd. Larceny. Forty days' detention 4/5/36 C.320/36
                                Released 10/6/36.
    As it is apparent the accused and his accomplice
were attempting to commit theft (possibly only the
theft of the brass pad-lock) when they were observed
breaking the lock at 445 Race Course Road; the accused
has been charged accordingly. The charge sheets will
be sent to the Court on the a.m. 26/3/41 for endorse-
ment and a remand requested.
    Regarding the Police on night duty at the scene of
the crime. Three C.P.C.'s were posted as follows :-
C.P.C. 3010 on duty at the front door 445 Race Course
Road, C.P.C.'s 1208 and 2939 on duty at the back door
of the radio station, located inside Lane 429 Race
Course Road (approached from Chungking Road). The
page_data.zh:
1/6.

    副督察（D.P.S.）83号 Cockburn 将两枚在现场发现的弹壳和射出的子弹，连同华捕巡长2165号的配枪（工部局警务处编号1638），一并送至武器鉴定科进行检查。结果报告将在适当时候收到。
    被告的指纹也被送至指纹局，经查有以下前科记录：
    因盗窃罪出庭。拘留四十天，1936年5月4日，案件号 C.320/36
                                1936年6月10日释放。
    由于明显看出被告及其同伙在被发现撬动跑马厅路445号门锁时正企图行窃（可能仅是盗窃黄铜挂锁），已据此对被告提出指控。起诉书将于1941年3月26日上午送交法庭背书，并申请还押候审。
    关于案发地点夜间执勤的警察情况。三名华捕巡长部署如下：华捕巡长3010号在跑马厅路445号前门执勤，华捕巡长1208号和2939号在广播电台后门执勤，该后门位于跑马厅路429弄内（从重庆路进入）。

page_data.en:
1/7.

latter were at their posts and ran around to Race
Course Road on hearing the shots fired but arrived
too late to take any part in the action.
C.P.C. 3010 who was supposed to be on guard at
the front entrance had arrested a male Chinese on
Race Course Road at 5.10 a.m. 25/3/41 and left his
post to take this man to the station, where latter was
subsequently charged with larceny by climbing (F.I.R.
352/41). Nevertheless, it is readily apparent that
C.P.C. 3010 spent more time in the station, than was
required for the job in hand, as he did not return to
his post until after 6.40 a.m. 25/3/41 when the
shooting occurred. On the instructions of the D.C.
(Divisions) C.P.C. 3010 has been posted as a defaulter.
Statements of P/C C.P.C. 2165, C.P.C.'s 1208,
2939 and 3010 are attached to this file.
Enquiries proceeding.

后两人在听到枪声时虽在岗，但跑至跑马厅路时已太晚，未能参与行动。
本应在前门守卫的华捕巡长3010号，于1941年3月25日凌晨5时10分在跑马厅路逮捕了一名中国男子，并离开岗位将该男子送往警局，后者随后被控以爬墙盗窃罪（首次调查报告号 352/41）。然而，显而易见的是，华捕巡长3010号在警局停留的时间超过了处理此事所需的时间，因为他直到1941年3月25日上午6时40分枪击发生后才返回岗位。根据分区副督察（D.C. (Divisions)）的指示，华捕巡长3010号已被记为失职。
华捕巡长2165号、华捕巡长1208号、2939号和3010号的陈述附于本案卷宗。
调查正在进行中。

C.P.C. 2165 Jau Zau Yuin, states as follows:-

Between 11 p.m. 24-3-41 and 7 a.m. 25-3-41, I was detailed
for duty in plain clothes, patrolling Race Course Road.

At about 6.35 a.m. 25-3-41, as I was patrolling West along
Race Course Road on the North side of the roadway, I observed
two male Chinese who were in the act of forcing open the front
door of No. 445 Race Course Road, the premises of X.W.H.A.
Radio Station.

I immediately drew out my service pistol, and warned them
not to move. However they ignored my warning, and ran East
(on Race Course Road) in order to make their escape. I chased
after them and at the same time shouted to them that if they
continued to run, I would open fire, but neither of them paid
any attention.

Observing that they were about to turn into Mohawk Road
and being afraid that they would succeed in making good their
escape, I was obliged to fire a shot as a last warning. They
still failed to stop so I fired a 2nd shot which took effect,
hitting one of the men.

The injured man was stopped by C.D.C. 84 (attached to
Yangtzepoo Station) near house No. 61 Mohawk Road, whilst
his accomplice made good his escape. I left the injured man
in the care of the above C.D.C. and proceeded to the Mohawk Rd.-
Ave Rd. VII Street Telephone box, where I telephoned to the
station to report the case.

A few moments later, a party of Police arrived and the
injured man was removed to the hospital in an ambulance.

Three pad-locks were found on the person of the arrested
person.

Signed:-
page_data.zh:
华捕巡长（C.P.C.）2165号 Jau Zau Yuin（音译）。
华捕侦探警佐（C.D.S.）192号
成都路警局           1941年3月25日        翻译   文员 Weng。

华捕巡长（C.P.C.）2165号 Jau Zau Yuin（音译），陈述如下：

1941年3月24日晚上11时至1941年3月25日上午7时之间，我被指派便衣执勤，在跑马厅路巡逻。

1941年3月25日上午6时35分左右，当我沿跑马厅路北侧向西巡逻时，我观察到两名中国男子正在强行打开跑马厅路445号X.W.H.A.广播电台处所的前门。

我立即拔出配枪，警告他们不许动。然而他们无视我的警告，向东（沿跑马厅路）逃跑以图脱身。我追赶他们，同时向他们喊话，若继续奔跑我将开枪，但两人均未理会。

见他们即将转入莫霍克路，且担心他们会成功逃脱，我被迫开了一枪作为最后警告。他们仍未停下，于是我开了第二枪，击中其中一人。

受伤男子在莫霍克路61号房屋附近被华捕侦探（C.D.C.）84号（隶属杨树浦警局）拦停，而其同伙则成功逃脱。我将伤者交由上述华捕侦探看管，随即前往莫霍克路与爱德华七世大道交叉口的街头电话亭，打电话向警局报告此案。

片刻后，一队警察赶到，伤者由救护车送往医院。

在被捕者身上发现了三个挂锁。

签名：-

No. 145 Race Course Road.
    Between 11 p.m. 24-3-41 and 3 a.m. 25-3-41, I was on
duty outside the front entrance of the premises (on Race
Course Road. From 3 a.m. 25-3-41 I was on duty outside the

C.P.C. 3010 Jung Kwang Hoo states as follows:-
Between 11 p.m. 24-3-41 and 7 a.m. 25-3-41, C.P.C.s
1293, 2039 and I were detailed for duty at No. 445 Race
Course Road, the R.H.A. Radio Station.
Between 11 p.m. 24-3-41 and 7 a.m. 25-3-41, I was on
duty outside the back door of the premises (Lane 429
Race Course Road) and from 7 a.m. I started to be on duty
outside the front entrance (on Race Course Road).
At 5.10 a.m. 25-3-41, I observed a male Chinese
carrying several articles of clothing in his hand. As
his actions appeared to be suspicious, I took him in
custody and brought him to the station.
Later I accompanied the Chinese detective to No.
370 Race Course Road, where the complainant was located,
and we returned to the station. I then went to the lavatory
to relieve nature.

page_data.en:
RADIO FLASH
September 11th, 1941

NO! It's Not A Mistake
Ten days ago XCDN's overwrought staff
admitted defeat and announced the station
would be off the air for a weekend. This was not
according to the plan which laid down uninterrupted broadcasting through and despite the
turmoil of the installation of short-wave (it had
been installed earlier but there were still finishing
touches to be added) and the removal of the studios
to a new location. A period of silence was declared and technicians at work on the control
panel heaved a sigh of relief, able at last to fit
gadgets and unravel acres of wire without falling
over shoosh-ing announcers at every turn.
The new studios opened, bright painted name-
plate on the door. Immediately came a chorus
of "What? G? Surely a misprint!" Truth
would out; after over a year's operation on medium
wave, it had suddenly occurred to the experts
that XC—was a Mexican call-sign. China's official
allocation is from XG—and on. This had not
mattered much so long as the station was audible
locally only, but the coming of short-wave conjured up visions of radio tangles and misunderstandings in the Antilles, Antipodes and what-have-you if we continued to wear the Mexican
disguise. So XCDN became a thing of the past.
The temptation to have XVVV was great but the
vision of an announcer trying to enunciate the
three V's clearly put the idea out of court. XGDN
was the closest phonetic approximation to the
old call-sign.
XCDN hail and farewell! XGDN is calling!

FILE
page_data.zh:
无线电快讯
1941年9月11日

不！这不是错误
十天前，XCDN 疲惫不堪的工作人员
承认失败，并宣布电台将停播一个周末。这并不
符合原定计划，该计划规定尽管在安装短波设备（此前已安装，但仍有一些收尾工作要做）和将演播室搬迁至新地点的过程中存在混乱，仍需保持不间断广播。一段静默期被宣布，控制台上的技术人员松了一口气，终于可以在不总是绊倒那些发出“嘘”声的播音员的情况下安装小装置并理顺成英亩计的电线。
新演播室开放，门上挂着漆得鲜亮的名牌。随即传来一阵“什么？G？肯定是印刷错误！”的合唱声。真相大白；在中波波段运营一年多后，专家们突然想到 XC— 是墨西哥的呼号。中国的官方分配是从 XG— 开始。只要电台仅在当地可收听，这并无大碍，但短波的到来让人联想到如果我们继续披着墨西哥的外衣，将在安的列斯群岛、大洋洲等地引发无线电纠纷和误解。因此 XCDN 成为过去式。
使用 XVVV 的诱惑很大，但想到播音员试图清晰发音三个 V 的画面，便打消了这个念头。XGDN 是在语音上最接近旧呼号的近似值。
XCDN 你好且再见！XGDN 正在呼叫！

SHANGHAI TIMES.

ALLIED BROADCAST
OVER XCDN

B. R. A. Protest Stopping
Of Medical Supplies
To Hankow British

At the regular fortnightly meeting of the General Committee of the British Residents' Association of China held on Tuesday afternoon, reference was made to the recent establishment of an Allied Federation Committee to consolidate allied activities in Shanghai, especially publicity, and to cement the bond of union between the allies.
In this connection it was mentioned that there would be an allied broadcast over station XCDN commencing at 7.40 p.m., today. The Chairman of the B.R.A. was nominated to represent the Association on the Federation Committee.
Information had been received from Hankow that owing to the refusal of the Japanese authorities to permit shipment of essential supplies, the Hankow Dispensary Ltd. had been obliged to close down. The Hankow Dispensary Ltd. is the only British concern of its kind in that port, and its closure creates a serious situation for the British community, being a direct menace to health. The matter is to be taken up in the proper quarters.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。

盟国通过 XCDN 电台广播

英侨会抗议停止向汉口英人供应医疗物资

在周二下午举行的在华英侨会总委员会例行双周会议上，提及最近成立了一个盟国联合会委员会，以巩固盟国在上海的活动，特别是宣传工作，并加强盟国之间的团结纽带。
在此方面，有人提到，将于今晚7时40分起通过 XCDN 电台进行盟国联合广播。英侨会主席被提名为代表该协会参加联合会委员会。
从汉口收到消息，由于日本当局拒绝允许运送必要物资，汉口大药房有限公司（Hankow Dispensary Ltd.）被迫关闭。汉口大药房有限公司是该港口唯一的此类英商企业，其关闭给英侨社区造成了严峻局面，直接威胁到健康。此事将在适当层面提出交涉。

CHINA PRESS
APR 27 1940
Temporary Schedule
British Radio
Station Here
Goes Off Air
The new British broadcasting
station here, which was the object
of concerted interference by a rival
station, went off the air completely
yesterday, although officials declar-
ed that the interference was not
the cause of the temporary closing-
down.
"Organization" was given as the
reason why the station did not
broadcast yesterday. "The station
is still in an embryonic stage," it
was said, "and various changes
must be made after the trial period
during which it was on the air."
Station XMHD was not inter-
fered with yesterday or the day
before. Reports printed in yester-
day's edition were erroneous, re-
ference being made instead to the
new British station, which has not
yet been given a name or call-
letters.
The rival station which blotted
out the new British station's pro-
grams was believed by informed
quarters to be located in Hongkew.
No interference with the American-
owned station, XMHA, has been
noted for several days, although
this station was the original target
in the "radio war."

停播原因归结为“组织调整”。据悉，“该台仍处于初创阶段，在试播期间必须进行各种调整。”
XMHD 电台昨日及前日均未受到干扰。昨日版刊印的报道有误，其所指实为这家尚未获得名称或呼号的新英国电台。
据知情人士认为，抹除新英国电台节目的 rival 电台位于虹口。尽管美资电台 XMHA 是“无线电战”的最初目标，但数日来未注意到对该台的干扰。

CHINA PRESS.
APR 26 1941

Programs Blotted Out
XMHD Is Now
Object Of
Interference

Interference with radio stations
in Shanghai yesterday spread to
XMHD, Shanghai Christian Broad-
casting Association station at 128
Museum Road. Many of the broad-
casts in the morning and afternoon
were blotted out entirely for Shang-
hai listeners.
Meanwhile, no interference at all
with the American-owned station,
XMHA, was reported, although its
broadcasts were the original target
of persons who attempted to halt
reception here.
The interference with XMHD, as
in the case of XMHA, was believed
to have originated in Hongkew. A
rival radio station situated some-
where in that area allegedly is try-
ing to jam news broadcasts especial-
ly, since these might be held to be
"anti-Japanese."
No other reason seems to be
known for the interference with
XMHD. However, the 9 p.m. news
program was not jammed last
night.
Action in the form of protests to
the Japanese Consulate-General
here might be taken, it was believ-
ed, following the lead of the officials
of XMHA, who filed a protest with
the American Consulate-General,
which made representations with
the Japanese Consul. The North-
China Daily News, British-owned
newspaper, uses XMHD for several
news programs during the day, but
it was not known yesterday whe-
ther the British authorities would
be appealed to.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1941年4月26日

节目被抹除
XMHD 现成为
干扰对象

昨日上海的无线电电台干扰蔓延至位于博物馆路128号的上海基督教广播协会电台 XMHD。上海听众早晨和下午的许多广播节目被完全抹除。
与此同时，据报道美资电台 XMHA 未受到任何干扰，尽管其广播曾是试图阻止此处接收信号者的最初目标。
人们认为，对 XMHD 的干扰与 XMHA 的情况一样，源自虹口。据说位于该区域某处的一个 rival 广播电台正试图特别干扰新闻广播，因为这些新闻可能被视为“反日”。
似乎没有已知的其他原因解释对 XMHD 的干扰。然而，昨晚9点的新闻节目未受干扰。
据信，继 XMHA 官员向美国总领事馆提出抗议（美方随后向日本领事提出交涉）之后，可能会采取向驻沪日本总领事馆提出抗议的行动。《字林西报》这家英资报纸白天利用 XMHD 播放数个新闻节目，但昨日尚不清楚是否会向英国当局求助。

Date 14 3 40

NCDN Undecided
To Build Radio
Station Again

THE question of the
North-China Daily News
running its own radio station
is still "in, not on the air"
the Shanghai Evening Post was
informed this morning.
Persistent reports in Shang-
hai to the effect that the
senior British morning paper
was once again to own a
transmitter were due to "the
fact that NCDN had been con-
sidering such a move for the
past year or so, but was still
doubtful on the matter.
NCDN owned and operated
its own station some 15 years
ago. At present it is giving
daily news broadcasts from
the transmitter of XMHD, the
Christian Broadcasting Asso-
ciation station.

上海公共租界工部局警务处

日期 1940年3月14日

《字林西报》尚未决定
再次建造广播电台

《上海晚邮报》今晨获悉，《字林西报》运营自有广播电台的问题仍“处于筹备中，尚未开播”。
上海流传甚广的说法称，这份资深英资晨报将再次拥有发射机，这源于“《字林西报》在过去一年左右一直在考虑此举，但对此事仍存疑虑”这一事实。
《字林西报》曾在约15年前拥有并运营自己的电台。目前，它通过基督教广播协会电台 XMHD 的发射机每日播放新闻广播。

(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S.B. REGISTRY No. B.D. Date)

With reference to the request of one Clyde A. Geist
for authority to open a radio broadcasting station, it is
learned that this individual is an American citizen, registered
at the American Consulate-General, born on January 27, 1905,
and is the possessor of an American passport No. 462482
issued in Washington.

In July 1937, Geist retired from the U.S. Navy after
sixteen years service and subsequently became attached to
the U.S. Naval Reserve. Following his resignation from
the Navy, Geist returned to Shanghai which he had visited
on numerous occasions during the course of his naval service
on August 7, since which date he has resided at 1280 Avenue
Road, living with a Cantonese girl to whom he refers as his
wife. From the above address, Geist has very successfully
operated an amateur radio station and it is worthy of note
that during the period of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in
the Shanghai area, this station was responsible for the
transmitting of many messages to places as far afield as
Manila, as many local residents can testify.

On February 22, 1938, Geist opened a shop for a radio
repair service located at 1249 Bubbling Well Road under the
name of Radio City Service. In the running of this business,
Geist is assisted by one Russian radio mechanic whose name
has not yet been ascertained.

With regard to the radio broadcasting station, call
sign XERC, it is learned that Geist hopes to have this in
operation by the end of May, 1938, though he has not as yet

关于 Clyde A. Geist 请求批准开设广播电台一事，据悉此人为美国公民，在美国总领事馆注册，出生于 1905 年 1 月 27 日，持有在华盛顿签发的美国护照，号码为 462482。

Geist 于 1937 年 7 月在服役十六年后从美国海军退役，随后加入美国海军预备役。辞去海军职务后，Geist 返回上海，他在海军服役期间曾多次访问上海，自 8 月 7 日以来，他一直居住在爱文义路 1280 号，与一名他称为妻子的广东女子同住。从上述地址，Geist 非常成功地运营着一个业余无线电台，值得注意的是，在上海地区中日敌对行动期间，该电台负责向远至马尼拉等地发送许多信息，许多当地居民可以作证。

1938 年 2 月 22 日，Geist 在静安寺路 1249 号开设了一家名为“无线电城服务处”的无线电维修店。在经营这项业务中，Geist 得到了一名俄罗斯无线电技师的协助，其姓名尚未查明。

关于呼号为 XERC 的广播电台，据悉 Geist 希望能在 1938 年 5 月底前投入运营，尽管他尚未

Date Dec. 8, 19 38.
Subject Letter from Major Asano re Tien Zeur Radio Broadcasting
Station (XQHG) K.C. 1300 - K.C.1300 already reserved by
Swiss owned Liang Yue Broadcasting Station (XQCT)
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by

With reference to the attached letter, dated
6.12.38 addressed to the Police Department, Shanghai
Municipal Council, by Major Kazuwo Asano, of the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, which states that permission has
been granted to the Tien Zeur Radio Broadcasting Station
(XQHG) located at 701 Foochow Road, to broadcast over a
carrier frequency wavelength of K.C.1300, it should be
noted that K.C.1300 has already been adopted by the Swiss
owned (Mr. J.V. Saunier) Liang Yue Broadcasting Station
(XQCT) with the consent of the Swiss Consul-General. Mr.
Saunier's station was in operation before anything was
heard from the Japanese of the Tien Zeur Station.

It will be noted that according to Major Asano's
letter, a German, Mr. F.W. Wettengel, is the owner of the
new station. Information in the possession of the Special
Branch, however, is to the effect that the Tien Zeur Station
is really the property of one Liu Tsung-san (刘春山), a
local comedian who, since the fall of Shanghai to the
Japanese Forces, has been employed by the Japanese as a
radio comedian. Mr. Wettengel is stated to be a German
in poor financial circumstances, who along with several
other Germans, occupies Room 2A, Yokohama Specie Bank Building,
24 The Bund. No application has been received by the
Shanghai Municipal Police from Wettengel in respect of the
Tien Zeur Station. In view of the fact that he is not
of a nationality which enjoys extra-territorial rights, it
would appear that before his station is permitted to operate,
he should be required to furnish the usual guarantee

关于附上的由广播监理所浅野一雄（Kazuwo Asano）少校于1938年12月6日致上海公共租界工部局警务处的信件，信中指出已准许位于福州路701号的天蟾广播电台（XQHG）使用K.C.1300载波频率波长进行广播，须注意的是，K.C.1300已被瑞士人（J.V. Saunier先生）拥有的良友广播电台（XQCT）采用，并已获得瑞士总领事的同意。Saunier先生的电台在日本方面提及天蟾电台之前就已投入运营。

值得注意的是，根据浅野少校的信件，新电台的所有者是一名德国人F.W. Wettengel先生。然而，特科掌握的信息显示，天蟾电台实为本地滑稽戏演员刘春山（Liu Tsung-san）所有，自上海被日军占领以来，他一直被日本人雇佣为广播滑稽戏演员。据称Wettengel先生是一名经济状况不佳的德国人，与其他几名德国人一起，占据外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼的2A室。上海公共租界警务处未收到Wettengel关于天蟾电台的任何申请。鉴于他不属于享有治外法权国籍的人士，在其电台获准运营之前，似乎应要求他提供通常由中国运营的广播电台所提供的保证

not to broadcast any political matter. Information has
been received to the effect that the new station commenced

The following is a brief outline of information
supplied to the Special Branch by Mr. J.V. Saunier, owner
of the Liang Yue Station (XQST) K.C.1300, who called at
Headquarters at 11.30 a.m. December 8, viz :- On September
21, 1938, Mr. Saunier inserted an advertisement in the Sin
Wen Pao to the effect that he had established the Liang Yue
Broadcasting Station (X.Q.C.T.) K.C.1300, but did not
receive any objection until October 20, 1938, when he
received a letter from the Superintendence Office ordering
his station to close down. After consultation with his
Consul-General, Mr. Saunier sent a reply to the Japanese on
October 21, 1938, asserting his right to continue to broadcast
over K.C.1300.
Nothing further was heard by Mr. Saunier from the
Japanese until November 21, 1938, when at the request of
Mr. Ban (Japanese) of the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, he kept an appointment with the latter. The inter-
view did not result in a satisfactory settlement, but Mr.
Ban suggested as a solution that Mr. Saunier might adopt any
of the following wavelengths, viz :-
K.C. 720
K.C. 800
K.C. 840
K.C. 980

以下是良友电台（XQST）K.C.1300的所有者J.V. Saunier先生向特科提供的信息概要，他于12月8日上午11:30来到总部，具体如下：- 1938年9月21日，Saunier先生在《新闻报》上刊登广告，声明他已建立良友广播电台（X.Q.C.T.）K.C.1300，但直到1938年10月20日才收到异议，当时他收到监理所的一封信，命令其电台关闭。在与他的总领事协商后，Saunier先生于1938年10月21日向日本方面发出回复，主张其继续在K.C.1300上广播的权利。
在此之后，直到1938年11月21日，Saunier先生未再从日本方面听到任何消息，当时应广播监理所Ban先生（日本人）的要求，他与后者进行了会面。这次会谈并未达成令人满意的解决方案，但Ban先生提出作为解决方案，Saunier先生可以采用以下任一波长，即：-
K.C. 720
K.C. 800
K.C. 840
K.C. 980

Mr. Saunier promised to consider the matter but
upon making enquiries, learned that K.C.800, K.C.840 and
K.C.980 were wavelengths adopted by Chinese stations which
had failed to register with the Superintendence Office,
while K.C.720 was adopted by the Kien Wah Station (Note
This station has since changed to K.C.740 at the request
of the Japanese with whom it is registered, but Mr. Saunier,
fearing further interference, refused to budge from the
original wavelength, i.e. K.C.1300 adopted by him).
On November 22, 1938, the Swiss Consul-General
addressed a letter to the Japanese Authorities to the
effect that Mr. Saunier would continue to broadcast over
K.C.1300.
In the course of his conversation Mr. Saunier stated
that despite the fact that the Tien Zeur Station (Mr. Wettengel)
has commenced to broadcast, he will continue to operate the
Liang Yue Station even if it involves financial loss due to
confusion of wavelengths.

1938年11月22日，瑞士总领事致函日本当局，表示Saunier先生将继续在K.C.1300上广播。
在谈话过程中，Saunier先生表示，尽管天蟾电台（Wettengel先生）已开始广播，他将继续运营良友电台，即使这会导致因波长混淆而产生的经济损失。

REPORT Date November 5, 1938.

Subject New Broadcasting Station reported being installed in
Tien Chuan Theatre.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. [Signature]

At about 5 p.m. November 4, 1938, Mr. Koo Yang-luh
(過養祿), representing the Liang Yue Broadcasting Station,
K.Q.C.T., K.C. 1300, at 454 Nanking Road, which is Swiss
owned (Mr. Garnier), called at Special Branch, Headquarters
and supplied information to the effect that a new broadcasting
station is being installed in the Tien Chuan Theatre,
Foochow Road, which, it is believed, will operate on the
same frequency as that of the Liang Yue Station. He stated
that he would like to be advised as to whether he would
be entitled to continue to broadcast over the frequency of
K.C. 1300 if it was true that the Japanese had allocated
the same frequency wave length to the new station.

It is to be noted that the Liang Yue Station was
established on the written authority of the Swiss Consul-
General, therefore the police have little control over it.

A visit to the Tien Chuan Theatre at 5.45 p.m. November
4 discovered that the new station is actually in the course
of construction, the antenna having been set up. It is
expected that the station will be ready to broadcast within
the next few days.

It was learned from a fitter in the employ of the
Theatre that the transmitter to be used was a second hand one
and that the principal sponsor of the station is Liu Tsung-
san (劉春山), a comedian, who, it is stated, has already
obtained permission from the Japanese Broadcasting Super-
intendence Office to operate a station on K.C. 1300. Liu
Tsung-san (劉春山) is believed to have been working in the

撰写人 特科督察长 Logan 转呈人 C. [签名]

1938年11月4日下午5点左右，代表位于南京路454号、由瑞士人（Garnier先生）拥有的良友广播电台（K.Q.C.T.，K.C. 1300）的顾养禄（Koo Yang-luh）先生来到总部特科，提供信息称，福州路天蟾大戏院内正在安装一个新的广播电台，据信该电台将与良友电台使用相同的频率。他表示，如果日本方面确实将相同的频率波长分配给新电台，他希望被告知是否有权继续在K.C. 1300频率上广播。

需要注意的是，良友电台是依据瑞士总领事的书面授权建立的，因此警方对其控制力有限。

11月4日下午5点45分对天蟾大戏院的访问发现，新电台实际上正在建设中，天线已经架设。预计该电台将在未来几天内准备好广播。

Subject Ya Kai (亞開) Broadcasting Station, 84 Fokien Road
(XQHT, K.C.1060) supercedes Commercial Broadcasting
Station, 405 Tientsin Road.
Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by

On October 1, 1939, an advertisement announcing
the inauguration of a new broadcasting station called
the Ya Kai Broadcasting Station, 84 Fokien Road (Call-
sign XQHT and Frequency 1060 K.C.) appeared in the
Chinese evening papers.
Enquiries show that the new station has
superceded the Commercial Broadcasting Station, 405
Tientsin Road, same call sign and wave length,
permission to do so having been obtained by Mr. L.F.
Jovino, an Italian and licensee of the former station,
from the Broadcasting Superintendente Office, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road. The Chinese manager of the
new station is one named Zee Ching (徐聲). Yuen
Voong Chu (袁鳳), former manager of the old station,
has severed connections with the organization. In
response to a request from Special Branch, Mr. Jovino
sent the attached letter dealing with the reorganization
in question.
It is to be noted that the Ya Kai Station
was originally the Dah Fang Station, the manager of
which named V. Chieri, an Italian subject, applied
to the Municipal Police to operate a radio station
on frequency 880 K.C. in June, 1939 but was later
instructed by the Italian Consulate General to cease
his attempts in this matter.

(Vide reports
dated 20.6.39
and 16.8.39)

D.W. Mac Adie
D.S.I.
..C. (Special Branch)

经查询，该新电台已取代位于天津路405号的商业广播电台，使用相同的呼号和波长。前电台持照人、意大利人 L.F. Jovino 先生已从南京路哈同大楼的广播监理处获得许可。新电台的中方经理名为徐聲（Zee Ching）。原旧电台经理袁鳳（Yuen Voong Chu）已与该机构断绝关系。应特别处的要求，Jovino 先生寄来了附信，说明有关重组事宜。

Subject. Commercial Broadcasting Station (Chung Ih) XQHT,
K.C.1000 - suspends broadcasting.
Made by. D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C

The Commercial Broadcasting Station, XQHT,
K.C.1000, an Italian owned concern located at Room 9,
2nd floor, 405 Tientsin Road, suspended broadcasting
at the end of September, 1938, ostensibly for the
purpose of renovating the transmitter. It is reported,
however, that the suspension was due, to some extent,
to dissension among the shareholders.

It is expected that the station will re-commence
broadcasting on November 16, 1938. The Chinese name
of the station will be changed from Chung Ih (中義)
to Jong Ih (商義), while its foreign name and
ownership will remain unchanged.

D. S. I.

Reference Special Branch report on above
subject, dated 20th June 1938, Mr. L. F. Jovino called
at Special Branch, Headquarters, on the morning of
14th July 1938, and stated that some days ago he
had been informed by his Consul to the effect that
the Broadcasting Superintendence Office (Japanese)
had been in touch with the Italian Consulate General
and had suggested that Mr. Jovino's Broadcasting
Station might perhaps broadcast Japanese propaganda.
The Italian Consulate General referred the Japanese
to Mr. Jovino stating that it was a matter which
the latter could decide. Mr. Jovino, at the request
of the Japanese, called at the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, Carlton Building, Nanking Road, at 10 a.m.,
14th July 1938, and was informed by Mr. Ban (Japanese)
that there was no objection to his operating a
radio broadcasting station. Mr. Ban then asked
Mr. Jovino if he would agree to broadcasting Japanese
propaganda, without however stating what form the
propaganda should take, but according to Mr. Jovino
he refused to have anything whatever to do with
the broadcasting of Japanese or any other propaganda.
Mr. Ban then informed him frequency K.C.
1000 which Mr. Jovino had been allowed for his
station had been reserved by the Japanese for their
own use and suggested that he should use a frequency

The attached translation is of a notice which appeared
in the June 16 issue of the Sin Wan Pao, intimating that
the Chung Ih Broadcasting Station (English official name -
Commercial Broadcasting Station) which is Italian owned, will
commence to operate as from 16/6/38. The call sign and fre-
quency is given as XQHT and K.C. 1000 respectively.
At 11.30 a.m., 18/6/38, Mr. Huang Tsze Chu (黃樹洲),
compradore of L. F. Jovino & Co., called at Special Branch,
Headquarters, and produced a certificate issued by the Acting
Consul General for Italy, dated 4/6/38, which states that the
Commercial Broadcasting Station, call sign XQHT, K.C. 1000 is
owned by Mr. Leopoldo Felice Jovino, an Italian subject
residing at 503 Dixwell Road. The station, which is located
on the 3rd floor of 405 Tientsin Road, will broadcast
commercial advertisements and musical items. It is due to
commence broadcasting on 10/7/38. The manager will be Mr.
Huang Tsze Chu aforesaid and the operator Mr. Cha Nan Shing
(邵乃興).
Reference Special Branch report dated 28/5/38, frequency
K.C. 1000 has been adopted by the Dollar Radio Station, a
Chinese owned concern which has not yet commenced to operate
and which has up to date not applied to the S.M.P. for
registration.
Mr. Jovino was interviewed at Special Branch, Headquarters,
on 20/6/38, when he stated that he would broadcast news

Subject Mr. P.H. Vanmeter (American), owner of the American
Commercial Broadcasting Station (XMHE) K.C.780,
reports that Japanese threaten to damage his station.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Gaspard

With reference to the dispute existing between
Mr. Vanmeter on the one hand and the Japanese Broadcasting
Superintendence Office and the Yeu Lien (Union) Broadcasting
Station (XHHV) which has been assigned the same wavelength
as Mr. Vanmeter's Station by the Japanese, on the other,
Mr. Vanmeter visited Headquarters, at 12 noon December 12,
1938, and reported that information had reached him that
members of the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office
had threatened to damage his station. Mr. Vanmeter did
not divulge how the information reached him but he affirmed
his determination to proceed with his intention to broadcast
over a frequency wavelength of K.C.780, and stated that as
he had the support of his Consul-General he would, if
provoked, consider increasing the power of his station much
beyond the 100 watts generally used in Shanghai.
Note It is understood that the Japanese are particularly
anxious that no station may exceed 100 watts in power.
Mr. Vanmeter's station is located at Room 266,
131 Hoopeh Road. He stated that as soon as he is ready to
commence broadcasting, he will inform the Police by letter.

Logan
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Subject Letter from Mr. P.H. Vanmeter, owner of The American Commercial Broadcasting Station intimating change of frequency
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. [签名]

With reference to the attached letter, dated
December -, 1938, addressed to the D.C. (Special Branch),
by Mr. P.H. Vanmeter, owner of the American Commercial
Broadcasting Station, which states that the location of
the Station has been changed from Lane 97, House 36,
Lyburgh Road to 131 Hupeh Road and that the frequency
wave-length over which the Station will broadcast is to
be changed from K.C. 780 to K.C.800.

It will be noted that K.C.800 is the frequency
wave-length over which the Sun Sun Radio Station broadcasts.
The Sun Sun Radio Station operates on Ministry of
Communications private radio station permit No.26 dated
October 31st, 24th Year of the Republic of China (1935)
and is one of the few stations remaining which had not
registered with the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 7 DEC 1933）
Mr. Vanmeter was interviewed at the Special Branch
at 2 p.m., December 5, 1938, when he stated that he had
been asked by a Japanese representative of the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office to change the frequency wave-length
of his station from K.C.780 to K.C.800 and at the same time
assured that provided he changed the frequency wavelength
as desired there would be no further interference by the
Japanese. Mr. Vanmeter mentioned also that the Japanese
who interviewed him, hinted that should the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office make a complaint to the S.M.P. in
regard to his station the S.M.P. would have no other course
but to close it down.

Vanmeter 先生于1938年12月5日下午2时在特科接受问询，当时他表示，日本广播监理局的一名代表要求他将电台的频率波长从 K.C.780 变更为 K.C.800，并同时保证，只要他按要求更改频率波长，日本人就不会再进行干扰。Vanmeter 先生还提到，采访他的日本人暗示，如果广播监理局就其电台向上海公共租界警务处投诉，警务处将别无选择，只能将其关闭。

Upon it being made known to Mr. Vanmeter that the
Sun Sun Radio Station is operating on a frequency wavelength
of K.C.800 on the authority of a permit issued by the
Ministry of Communications of the Nationalist Government
of China, he immediately stated that he would abandon his
intention to use K.C.800 and would revert to K.C.780 which
was originally chosen by him.

Despite the fact that Mr. Vanmeter emphatically
denied that any Chinese are financially interested in the
Station, information from other sources is to the effect
that one Hsu Ching-sien (許勁先) until recently Manager
of the Sun Sun Radio Station and concurrently owner/manager
of the Hwa Shin Broadcasting Station (XNHP, N.C.19 Tsingtao
Road) is associated with Mr. Vanmeter in establishing the
new station. This man left the Sun Sun Radio Station in
consequence of a dispute which arose over the commission paid
to him and may well be harbouring a grudge against the Sun
Sun Radio Station Management. It is known that he registered
the Hwa Shin Station with the Japanese Superintendence
Office.

The studio of the new American Commercial Broadcasting
Station will be located in Room 288 of the Yuan Tung Hotel,
131 Hupeh Road. Installation is in progress at present and
it is expected that the station will be ready to operate by
December 10th, 1938. Mr. Vanmeter stated that before
commencing to operate he will notify the Special Branch
in writing.

D.G. (Special Branch).

D. S. I.

尽管 Vanmeter 先生坚决否认有任何中国人对该电台有财务利益关系，但来自其他渠道的信息表明，前声声广播电台经理、同时兼任华信广播电台（XNHP，北青岛路19号）业主/经理的许劲先（Hsu Ching-sien）与 Vanmeter 先生有关联，共同建立了新电台。此人因佣金纠纷离开声声广播电台，很可能对声声广播电台管理层怀恨在心。已知他已向日本监理局注册了华信电台。

THE AMERICAN COMMERCIAL BROADCASTING STATION
131 Hupeh Road
Shanghai, December 2nd, 1938

The Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Branch)
Shanghai

Dear Sir:

I have established the American Commercial Broad-
casting Station at No. 131 Hupeh Road instead of House
36, Lane 97, Myburgh Road, as I found this place more
suitable.

This station will operate on the frequency 800 k. c.
The reason I am using this frequency is because the
Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office advised
me to do so as there is no other station registered on
that frequency. There is, however, one station operating
on this frequency with an old permit from the Chinese
Government, but this permit call for a frequency of 780
k. c. only.

This station is registered at the U. S. Consulate
and also with the Broadcasting Superintendence Office.
The Japanese have promised to cause no trouble should I
operate on the frequency 800 k. c.

Should you desire any further information, I will
be glad to give it to you at any time.

Yours faithfully,

P. H. Vanneter
Proprietor

本台将在 800 k. c. 频率上运营。我使用此频率的原因是日本广播监理局建议我这样做，因为在该频率上没有其他注册电台。然而，确实有一个电台凭中国政府颁发的旧许可证在此频率上运营，但该许可证仅要求 780 k. c. 的频率。

本台已在美国领事馆及广播监理局注册。日本人承诺，如果我在 800 k. c. 频率上运营，不会制造麻烦。

Deputy Commissioner of Police
Shanghai

Dear Sir:

I beg to inform you that I have established a
Broadcasting Station at the above address and will
operate on or before December 15th, 1938. (But in
the meantime should I be able to secure more suit-
able premises, I will move the Station to same, but
will inform you of such change.)

The power of this station is 100 watts, and I
will broadcast on a wave length of 780. Call Sig-
nal is XMHE.

This station will be used for commercial pur-
poses only, and will not accept any news items of
any description whatsoever.

This station will be known as the American Com-
mercial Broadcasting Station, and is registered at
the American Consulate at Shanghai as such. The
Consul has not given me a certificate stating that
the station is registered as it was deemed unneces-
sary, but promised to confirm same to you, should
you desire (Mr. Engdol has charge of the registra-
tion).

Should you desire any further information on
this station, I will be glad to furnish it to you
at any time.

I am the proprietor of the Station.

Yours faithfully,
P. H. Varmeter

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    S.P. File No. ...
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT                        Date Nov. 28, 1938.

Subject Application by Mr. J.C. Bosustow (British) for permission
to establish a Radio Broadcasting Station.
Made by D.S.I. Logan          Forwarded by C. Crawford

With reference to the attached letter dated 25.11.38
addressed to the Commissioner of Police by Mr. J.C. Bosustow
(British), Rooms 401-403, 346 Szechuen Road, requesting
permission to operate a Radio Broadcasting Station in the
International Settlement, Mr. Bosustow was interviewed at
10.30 a.m. November 28, 1938, by D.S.I. Logan. It was
pointed out to Mr. Bosustow that the S.M.C. would neither
issue permission for the operating of the proposed station
nor would any steps be taken to prevent same. Mr. Bosustow
claimed that he would be solely responsible for the station
but admitted that he was subscribing only a third of the
capital to be invested in the station, i.e. $1000.00 and
that the remaining two thirds would be subscribed by two
Russians, namely Mr. C. Djaine of A.E. Levy & Co., 113
Kiukiang Road, and Mr. V. Yakovleff, a local radio mechanic.
The total capital will be $3,000.00. According to Mr. Bosustow,
the programme will be broadcast in the Russian language and
will be on a purely commercial basis, politics being strictly
excluded.

It was pointed out to Mr. Bosustow that the frequency
wavelength proposed by him i.e. K.C.675 is unsuitable, where-
upon he stated that he would broadcast over a frequency
wavelength of K.C.680.

Mr. Bosustow stated that as a matter of courtesy,
he intended to inform the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office of his intention to operate a radio station over
K.C.680.

（左侧批注：adopted by T. Lang）

Made by. D.S.I. Logan. Forwarded by.

The attached letter was received by D.C.
(Japanese) from Major K. Asano, Chief of the Radio
Broadcasting Control Office on June 10, 1939, and
passed, together with translation, to D.C. (Special
Branch). Major Asano complains that the Tung Fang
Radio Station (XHHG), K.C.1220, located in the Grand
Hotel, 120 Yu Ya Ching Road, has failed to register
with the Japanese Radio Broadcasting Control Office,
despite orders issued by the latter on March 31st and
April 20th, 1939, and requests the immediate closure
of the Tung Fang Station.

It should be mentioned that the ownership of
the Tung Fang Station was transferred from the original
Chinese owners to Charles Madar & Co., (British), 259
Kiangse Road, on December 2, 1938, particulars of the
deed of sale being registered with the British
Consulate-General.

On January 19, 1939, the Mei Sung Radio
Station (XQMS), K.C.1220, 423 Nanking Road, which is
registered with the Japanese Authorities in the name
of Y. Ikeda (Japanese), 453 Dixwell Road, was
established and commenced broadcasting on the same
wavelength as that used by the Tung Fang Station.

In view of the fact that the Tung Fang Station
is British owned, the Police are powerless to interfere.

D. S. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)

June 7. 1939.
Shanghai Municipal Police Force

Sir,

Request for Issue of Order for Closing of
Tung Fong Radio Broadcasting Station.

I have to express my thanks for your valuable
assistance rendered in controlling the radio broadcasting
stations in the International Settlement since this office
had taken over the rights of controlling radio waves in
March 1938, owing to the necessity of military operations
of the Japanese Army. As a result, considerable facilities
have been obtained in the course of our functioning and
the work is now gradually arriving at the final stage of
achieving its aim.

The Tung Fong Radio Broadcasting Station (calling
XHG frequency 1220 KC) at the Grand Hotel, 120 Yu Ya Ching
Road, failed to register with this office ignoring the orders
issued on March 31 and April 2nd, 1939. Later, it stopped
broadcasting temporarily, but at the beginning of June this
year it recommenced broadcasting without permission from
this office and has been operating up to the present.

With a view to giving them another and the last
chance for reconsidering themselves, they were dealt with
leniently and ordered to attend this office so as to caution
them, but failed to do so.

In the light of these circumstances, the above-
mentioned station could not but regarded as having abandoned
the rights of operating as an authorised radio broadcasting
station. The name of this station has therefore been struck
off from the registration book and permission was accordingly
given to operate under frequency 1220 KC to the Mei Sung

1939年6月7日。
上海公共租界工部局警务处

先生，

关于请求发布关闭东方广播电台命令的事宜。

自本办公室于1938年3月因日军军事行动之必要接管无线电波管制权以来，承蒙贵方在控制国际租界内广播电台方面给予宝贵协助，特此致谢。因此，我们在运作过程中获得了相当多的便利，工作正逐渐进入实现目标的最后阶段。

位于虞洽卿路120号大饭店的东方广播电台（呼号XHG，频率1220 KC）无视本办公室于1939年3月31日和4月2日发布的命令，未向本办公室注册。此后，该台曾暂时停止广播，但在今年6月初，未经本办公室许可又重新开播，并一直运营至今。

为了给他们最后一次重新考虑的机会，我们对其从宽处理，命令其来本办公室接受警告，但他们未能照办。

鉴于上述情况，不得不认为上述电台已放弃作为授权广播电台运营的权利。因此，该台名称已从注册簿中注销，并相应批准美声

page_data.en:
( 2 )
Radio Broadcasting Station ( ), which
had applied for registration taking proper
procedure. The Li Sung Radio Broadcasting Station
commenced broadcasting as from January 18, 1939.
The T...g Radio Broadcasting Station still
continue to operate and has been intentionally
attempting to interfere with the business of the
Li Sung Radio Broadcasting Station, an act which
is regarded to be most improper.
Since the establishment of this office a year or
so ago, 71 radio broadcasting stations (8 ) have
been registered. At this time when there is a
prospect of the whole control of radio waves being
effected in the near future, the existence of such an
anti-Japanese and unauthorised radio broadcasting
station, which is interfering with the business of
another lawful station by exercising illegal acts,
is not justified from the point of view of the control
of radio waves and the maintenance of public peace
and order in the settlement.
I should be much obliged if you would cause
steps to be taken for the immediate closing of the
Tung Sang Radio Broadcasting Station.

Signed: I. Ishino.
Chief of the Radio Broadcasting
Control Office.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )
广播电台（ ），该台已按适当程序申请注册。丽声广播电台自1939年1月18日起开始广播。
T...g 广播电台仍在继续运营，并一直故意试图干扰丽声广播电台的业务，此举被认为极不妥当。
自本办公室成立约一年以来，已有71家广播电台（8 ）完成注册。在目前有望于近期实现无线电波全面管制的时刻，存在这样一个反日且未经授权的广播电台，通过非法行为干扰另一合法电台的业务，从无线电波管制和维护租界公共治安的角度来看，都是没有正当理由的。
如蒙贵方采取措施立即关闭东声广播电台，我将不胜感激。

签名：I. Ishino。
无线电广播管制办公室主任。

nominated to represent the Associa-

from Hankow that owing to the re- 
fusal of the Japanese authorities to 
permit shipment of essential 
supplies, the Hankow Dispensary 
Ltd. had been obliged to close 
down. The Hankow Dispensary 
Ltd. is the only British.concern of 
itskind in that port, and its closute 
creates a serious situation for the 
British community, being a direct 
menace to health. The matter is 
to be taken up in the proper 
quarters.
